RXV2-0.9.128-btn-clearance: Every page now starts its content just below the floating Home/Help buttons, so the bigger buttons no longer overlap titles, cards or text at the top of any screen.
RXV2-0.9.127-bigger-btns: Made the floating Home (🏠) and Help (?) buttons bigger — easier to spot and tap.
RXV2-0.9.126-home-btn: Every page now has a fixed home button (🏠, top-left, mirroring the ? help button) that jumps straight back to the front menu — no more scrolling to the bottom to find Return to menu. Shown on all screens except the home page itself.
RXV2-0.9.125-check-retry: Makes the firmware check robust to a transient blip: it now retries once (after the receiver has had a moment to settle its WiFi, e.g. just after a reboot) before giving up. Fixes the spurious 'Network error talking to the receiver' on the firmware page and makes the 'Update now?' dialog appear reliably.
RXV2-0.9.124-update-prompt: When you open a receiver, it now checks for newer firmware straight away and, if there is some, pops an 'Update now?' dialog (installed vs available shown) instead of just a banner. Tap Update now and it downloads, flashes and reboots itself, then returns to the home screen — one tap, no firmware page needed. The banner remains as a tap-to-update fallback; Later dismisses it. (The check still defers while a transmitter link is live, so it never interrupts flying.)
RXV2-0.9.123-fly-bind-guards: Two home-screen fixes. 'Fly now' now disables WiFi directly — one tap, with a friendly confirm that also shows your live link status (it used to just open a page where you had to find a second button). 'Start Bind mode' is now guarded: if the receiver is already bound/connected it warns before erasing the bind and dropping the link (so you can't do it by accident); unbound, it still binds straight away.
RXV2-0.9.122-status-led: Adds support for an external status LED on the D4 pad: OFF = bound but no link, ON = connected & receiving, 2 Hz flash = binding. Only active when transceiver 3 is absent (D4 is radio 3's CE on triple-radio boards, so those are unaffected — auto-detected). LED is assumed wired pad->resistor->LED->GND (active-high); tell me if yours is inverted.
RXV2-0.9.121-help-per-sim: The ? help on the controls & views screen now matches the simulator you opened: neXt gets its own help (its keys, why there are no Select/Up/Down buttons, and the Mac Input-Monitoring steps), RealFlight keeps its full controls-and-views help.
RXV2-0.9.120-simple-look: Cleaner look everywhere: all the tiny technical small print (ch 12 - 833us, F3, Keypad +, ...) is gone from the controls and the key buttons — just clear labels now. RealFlight's key buttons are the same bigger size as neXt's. (The key assigned to each button is still shown in the editor.)
RXV2-0.9.119-next-clean: neXt's screen no longer shows the Select/Up/Down/Cancel/Reset buttons — they're RealFlight User-Interface bindings and do nothing in neXt. The neXt key buttons are bigger to use the space (and the page skips the now-pointless button polling, kinder to the radio). RealFlight's screen is unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.118-nice-confirm: The are-you-sure box for starting/leaving simulator mode is now a friendly colourful card in the app's own style (with a big green Yes and a Cancel), replacing the browser's grey utilitarian confirm dialog. Tap outside it to dismiss.
RXV2-0.9.117-prof-front: The simulator choice now lives ONLY on the home screen: the RealFlight / neXt switch has been removed from the controls & views screen, whose title now simply shows which simulator is active (e.g. 'neXt — controls & views'). Tapping a home button always opens with the right key set; to change simulator, return to the menu.
RXV2-0.9.116-reboot-ux: No more white screen when toggling simulator mode: the phone now shows 'Rebooting — please wait...' immediately (drawn before the toggle is even sent, so it cannot blank), counts the seconds, then returns to the home screen by itself — with a Return-to-menu button there throughout. And the home menu now has TWO simulator buttons — RealFlight and neXt — each opening the controls & views screen with that simulator's key set selected.
RXV2-0.9.115-return-fix: Sim-mode toggle (and every other reboot page) now reliably returns to the home screen: a Return-to-menu button is always shown (one tap recovers it — never close-and-reload again), polling starts sooner and waits longer, the redirect dodges stale caches, and coming back to a backgrounded tab re-checks immediately. Also the Simulator switch (RealFlight / neXt) above the camera buttons is now big and obvious with a 'Simulator:' label — it was too subtle to spot before.
RXV2-0.9.114-next-keys: The neXt profile now comes pre-filled with neXt 2.087's real keys (from its Settings -> Misc list): New model, Engine, Pause, Self level, Trainer, Piro trainer, Time scale, Set spawn, Prev model/scenery, Landing gear, flight Conditions 1-4, Mute, Music, Recorder, Screenshot, Chat, Menu. All editable per profile as before; anything you'd already saved for neXt is kept.
RXV2-0.9.113-sim-profiles: Two simulators, two key sets: new RealFlight / neXt chips above the camera buttons switch between separate view-key profiles, each remembered on the phone. RealFlight keeps its pre-filled keys (and your edits); neXt starts empty — select it and tap Edit view keys to add keys from neXt's keyboard list. Chosen deliberately over USB host auto-detection, which is unreliable (and wrong under a VM).
RXV2-0.9.112-mac-help: Help now covers using the simulator on a Mac (neXt etc.): quit the Keyboard Setup Assistant, and crucially enable your simulator in System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Input Monitoring (then restart it) — macOS hides the sticks from the sim until you do, because the device is part keyboard. Help-text only; no behaviour change.
RXV2-0.9.111-view-colours: Every camera/view button now has its own colour, so you can find a favourite by colour at a glance. Colours are fixed to each button slot (your favourite stays the same colour), and the editor shows each slot's colour dot.
RXV2-0.9.110-equal-pills: Select and Cancel are now each full-width — the same size as Reset; Up/Down triangles a touch smaller to make room.
RXV2-0.9.109-ctl-fill: Controls screen: all the buttons grow a little more to use the spare white space — wider/taller Up & Down triangles, taller Select/Cancel/Reset with larger text. Scroll behaviour unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.108-touch-fix: Scrolling fixed: a vertical swipe now scrolls the page even when it starts on the big Up/Down triangles (scrolling never fires them; a quick tap still does). Up/Down triangles made a bit smaller, Select/Cancel/Reset a bit bigger.
RXV2-0.9.107-big-ctl: Controls now FILL the first screen (huge Up/Down triangles + bigger Select/Cancel/Reset, with Reset full-width) so you can hit them without looking at the phone; scroll down for the views. Views expanded with RealFlight's other commands: Look at ground, Zoom reset, Follow/Pivot/Orbit cam, Next pit view, Zoom/Move mode, Kill engine, Flight failures, Screenshot, Record, Mute — all editable, and your earlier key edits are kept. Also fixes the Up/Down labels overlapping.
RXV2-0.9.106-ctl-size: Tuned the RealFlight controls & views screen: bigger controls — especially the Up/Down triangles — so you can hit Up/Down repeatedly while watching the sim on a TV across the room, with the camera/view buttons made a little smaller to balance. Cosmetic only.
RXV2-0.9.105-rf-ui: RealFlight controls and Views are now ONE home-menu item opening a single screen: controls up top (Select/Cancel/Reset as smaller ovals, Up/Down as up/down triangles you press & hold to repeat), the camera/view buttons below, then a darker 'Edit view keys' button. Cosmetic only — same buttons, channels, keys and behaviour.
RXV2-0.9.104-edit-btn: Views page: moved the Edit button down below the camera buttons so it no longer sits under the top-right ? Help button. Nothing else changed — same buttons, keys and mappings.
RXV2-0.9.103-rf-views: Views page defaults are now RealFlight 9.5's real View Commands (read from its Keyboard Commands dialog): Chase/Fixed/Nose cam = F3/F1/F2, Cockpit = F4, Cycle cam = C, Zoom in/out = keypad +/-, Windsock = Up arrow. Tap 'Reset to defaults' to load them; the editor still lets you map any key/combo to any RealFlight command.
RXV2-0.9.102-views-editor: The Views page now has an on-screen Edit button: set each button's label and pick its key from a friendly dropdown (Ctrl/Shift/Alt too), Save — stored on the phone, no re-flashing. So you can map the buttons to RealFlight's real view shortcuts yourself.
RXV2-0.9.101-keyboard: Sim mode is now a USB composite device: the existing gamepad PLUS a standard keyboard. New 'Views (camera)' phone page sends keyboard shortcuts (next view, zoom, cockpit/chase, etc.) to RealFlight — keycodes editable in the page. Gamepad report unchanged (a one-time RealFlight re-detect of the composite device aside). Keystrokes are non-blocking and don't affect the channel rate.
RXV2-0.9.100-reset-ch10: Swapped Reset and Select channels: Reset now on channel 10 (a switchable channel on the transmitter), Select on channel 14. Reset is the one you most want on a physical switch. Channels now: 10=Reset, 11=Cancel, 12=Up, 13=Down, 14=Select; ch9 still free for autorotation.
RXV2-0.9.99-tap-reliable: Makes the RealFlight-controls phone buttons more reliable: a tap now fires 3 times over ~180 ms (so an occasional dropped WiFi request no longer loses the press), and the button pulse is longer (250 ms) so the sim can't miss the edge. The firmware merges the repeats into one clean press — never a multi-fire.
RXV2-0.9.98-reset-ch14: Moved the RealFlight-controls Reset button from channel 9 to channel 14 (joystick button 6), leaving channel 9 free for RealFlight's helicopter autorotation. Channels now: 10=Select, 11=Cancel, 12=Up, 13=Down, 14=Reset. Page-only change; no re-calibration. You'll need to put the Reset switch on TX ch14 and re-bind Reset in RealFlight.
RXV2-0.9.97-usb-revert: Reverts the 0.9.96 non-blocking USB write — it halved the TX frame rate while flying the sim (≈200 vs 500 with sim off). The blocking write yields the CPU and paces the loop, which the radio link needs. Back to the proven behaviour. Keeps the 'RealFlight controls' rename and the return-to-home fix.
RXV2-0.9.96-ui-polish: Front-menu 'Sim controls' renamed to 'RealFlight controls' (those buttons are RealFlight's UI functions). After toggling simulator mode, the reboot page now waits for the receiver to be solidly back before returning to the home screen, instead of landing on a blank page. Also makes the USB sim write non-blocking so it can't stall the loop.
RXV2-0.9.95-loop-diag: Diagnostic build: adds loop_hz (main-loop iterations/sec) and loop_max_us (worst loop stall) to /api/state.json, to tell a CPU/servicing limit from an RF problem when chasing dropped frames. No functional change.
RXV2-0.9.94-wifi-quiet: Sim mode now runs WiFi at much lower power (8.5 dBm vs 19.5) so it stops desensitising the nRF24 receiver sitting right beside it — the cause of the short range and dropped frames when driving the sim (WiFi and the TX link share 2.4 GHz). Should markedly lift the frame rate and range. Normal mode keeps full WiFi reach. No re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.93-bind-restore: Reverts the 0.9.92 loop change (servicing the radio 3x per loop), which disturbed the timing-sensitive bind/hop handshake and stopped the transmitter binding. Back to the proven 0.9.91 radio servicing. Keeps the lighter Sim-controls polling. Proper fix (a dedicated radio core) to follow.
RXV2-0.9.92-link-fix: Fixes a reluctant / flaky TX link when a web page was open during sim use. The radio is now serviced before AND after the web server (and after the USB sim write), so a slow web request can no longer make the receiver miss an FHSS hop or ack. The Sim controls page also polls 3x more gently and pauses when hidden. No re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.91-menu-fit: Sim controls: the Return-to-menu button is now full-width but a normal height, so the five function buttons (Select/Up/Down/Cancel/Reset) grow taller to fill the screen. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.90-pad-menu: Sim controls tidy-up: all six buttons now exactly the same size, with a full-size 'Return to menu' button at the bottom (the tiny top link is gone). Up is pale blue and Down dark blue for quick contrast. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.89-big-pad: Sim controls is now one tall column of big, easy-to-hit targets filling the screen, in order Select · Up · Down · Cancel · Reset — Reset largest at the bottom, like the spacebar. Same colours and Up/Down auto-repeat. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.88-sim-pad: Sim controls redesigned as a proper pad: big red Reset, green Select, amber Cancel, and a stacked ▲/▼ Up/Down rocker. Up and Down now AUTO-REPEAT — hold the on-screen button (or a TX switch on ch12/ch13) to scroll a menu continuously. Joystick descriptor unchanged (8 buttons), so no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.87-ui-buttons: Sim controls page now shows exactly RealFlight's 5 User Interface functions — Reset, Select, Cancel, Up, Down (ch9→Reset … ch13→Down) — instead of generic labels. The joystick is unchanged (still 8 HID buttons under the hood), so no re-calibration is needed.
RXV2-0.9.86-sim-buttons: Sim mode gains 8 function buttons on the USB joystick — fire them from the new 'Sim controls' phone page OR from your transmitter's switches on channels 9-16 (ch9→button1 … ch16→button8). Bind each to a sim function (reset, pause, view…) in your sim's controller setup, and control the sim with no keyboard. Adding buttons changes the joystick, so it needs one re-calibration in the sim.
RXV2-0.9.85-fresh-ui: Web pages are now sent no-store, so a freshly-updated UI appears immediately instead of the browser (iOS Safari especially) showing a stale cached copy — no hard-refresh needed.
RXV2-0.9.84-fs-auto: The receiver now derives its web-filesystem URL from the firmware URL when the page doesn't supply it, so it pulls its own web files on the next update even from a stale page — updating twice fully self-heals an out-of-date UI, no computer needed. Backups still preserved.
RXV2-0.9.83-fs-ota: OTA install now also flashes the matching web/data filesystem (and preserves your Rotorflight backups), so the web UI travels with the firmware on every update — no separate uploadfs needed. First release that ships a littlefs.bin.
RXV2-0.9.82-tx-happy: Firmware-update check no longer stalls the radio while the TX link is live (it was starving radioPoll and dropping the transmitter); shorter idle timeouts.
RXV2-0.9.81-wifi-heal: WiFi self-heals from AP-only — retries the home network every 20 s when it has saved credentials, instead of staying stranded. Plus a big SIMULATOR-MODE-ON home banner.
RXV2-0.9.80-sim-safe: Drive-simulator-over-USB now disables the flight-controller output (D6 stays silent) so a real model can't be flown from sim mode; default channel map shown as a tidy 1:1.
RXV2-0.9.79-usb-sim-remap: Adds the Remap-channels page for simulator mode (feed any of the 8 sim outputs from any received channel, with live bars).
RXV2-0.9.78-usb-sim: First release with Drive-simulator-over-USB: the receiver can present as a USB HID joystick for a PC flight sim, driven by the channels it receives — no separate dongle.
RXV2-0.9.224-crsf-rate: Adds a CRSF frame-rate setting on the Output protocol page (250/100/50 Hz). Lower it to 100 Hz for CRSF-to-PWM servo converters whose firmware misbehaves above ~100 Hz. Default stays 250 Hz. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.225-fc-telem-switch: New 'Flight controller on the telemetry line' switch on the Output protocol page. Untick it for plain CRSF-to-PWM servo converters: some echo junk that gets misread as telemetry (phantom current readings / false max-current alarms on the transmitter) — the receiver then ignores the telemetry line entirely and sends no Rotorflight probes. Default remains ON.
RXV2-0.9.226-async-update-check: The update check no longer blocks the receiver: manifest fetches now run in the background, so opening the app's front screen can't pause the servo output (the brief servo twitch with no transmitter connected). Results are cached for 10 minutes.
RXV2-0.9.227-vbat-adc: Receiver battery voltage on a spare pin: wire the pack through a 220k/10k divider (ratio 23.0, good to 12S; 100k/10k = 11.0 for 6S) + 100nF to D4 or D9 (free on 2-radio boards). Configure on the View-channels page; live volts (and per-cell if you set the cell count) shown there, and the voltage is sent to the transmitter as telemetry (12S pre-halve quirk handled).
RXV2-0.9.229-vbat-d9-only: Battery divider: D9 only (GPIO 8 — the one free pad on 2-radio boards; D4 carries the status LED), auto-detected when FC telemetry is off. IMPORTANT: replaces 0.9.227/228, which used wrong GPIO numbers for the divider pin (raw 9 = the SPI MOSI line!) — do not use those two versions with a divider.
RXV2-0.9.230-throttle-safe: SAFETY: the throttle channel (configurable on the Output protocol page, default 3) is held fully LOW (885 us) from power-on until the transmitter is actually heard — a receiver booted without its TX can no longer put the motor at half stick. Plus: booting with the TX already on now leaves Bluetooth open for 30 s (connect in that window and the link stays); and renaming the receiver from the app now works (inline rename box — the old popup was silently ignored by app WebViews).
RXV2-0.9.231-channels-tidy: Channel assignments consolidated: the arming channel now lives on the Output protocol page beside the throttle channel (one 'Channels' box); the arming card is gone from View channels. Battery card layout fixed so Pin/Ratio/Cells labels stay with their boxes on narrow phone screens.
RXV2-0.9.232-live-settings: Reboot only when it's actually needed: changing the CRSF rate, FC-telemetry switch, throttle channel or arming channel now applies instantly ('Saved — applied instantly' on the page, no reboot). Only changing the protocol itself (or PPM polarity) still reboots, because the output pin must be reconfigured.
RXV2-0.9.233-battery-save-dialog: Fixes the View-channels page broken in 0.9.231/232 (a script error meant Save battery settings did nothing and saved values weren't displayed — the settings themselves were never lost). Battery save now shows a proper 'Saved' confirmation dialog like the gear-ratio save.
RXV2-0.9.234-civilised-ota: Civilised OTA (Malcolm's word): when the connection drops during an install — routine over Bluetooth, and at the reboot moment on WiFi — the page no longer cries 'failed'. It says 'Installing… waiting for the receiver to come back', polls until the receiver reappears, and judges by the version it reports: new version = success (auto-reload), same old version = a real failure, still absent after 5 min = 'reload in a moment'.
RXV2-0.9.235-tx-failsafe: The transmitter's 'send failsafe to receiver' button now works on RXV2 (it was silently ignored): it captures the current channel positions — trims and subtrims included, since they're baked into the radio stream — exactly like the web 'Save failsafe' button. And with the FC-telemetry switch OFF (no flight controller, e.g. a PWM converter), the receiver now STREAMS the captured failsafe posture on CRSF after signal loss instead of going silent and letting the converter drift.
RXV2-0.9.236-install-clarity: Two update-flow niceties from Malcolm's hunting-lodge session: (1) trying to install while the receiver isn't on home WiFi now gets a plain explanation (the RECEIVER downloads the image itself, so the phone's internet can't help) instead of a cryptic failure; (2) an elapsed-time ticker during installs — the chip can't report true progress while flashing, but an honest count beats a frozen screen.
RXV2-0.9.237-bind-safe: SAFETY: the propeller could blip during a reboot-into-bind (prop fitted, hands near the model). Two defences: (1) every web-initiated reboot now pushes ~100ms of throttle-low frames and parks the output pin idle-high through the restart, so the converter/FC sees silence instead of noise; (2) the throttle stays pinned low until the link has delivered a stable stream (25 channel packets ≈ 0.5s) — covering the no-TX boot AND the first moments after binding, when a V1 transmitter in bind mode bypasses its own motor-low overrides.
RXV2-0.9.243-tidy-gaps-wave: Blackbox: TX switch-off no longer records a misleading final gap in saved flights. New: after the TX goes off, the receiver waves the ailerons when Bluetooth/WiFi become available.
RXV2-0.9.244-plane-blackbox: Blackbox now works on planes (no flight controller needed): flights record and save using the receiver's own battery divider. Adds radio swap count and per-transceiver time to flight stats. Includes the shutdown-gap trim and BLE aileron wave from 0.9.243.
RXV2-0.9.245-field-ble: Field mode is now Bluetooth-only (no more auto AP when home WiFi is absent; AP still available in WiFi settings). Update page explains the Bluetooth app path instead of claiming updates are impossible. Current-flight view no longer shows the TX switch-off as a scary longest gap. Flight graph: missing sensors greyed out, battery noise no longer magnified. Aileron wave now repeats on every landing of a session.
RXV2-0.9.246-ring-fix: Fixes the switch-off gap still showing (the trim ring was flooded by normal packets). Also skips the first seconds of battery sampling to kill a bogus 25V boot spike in the graph.
v0.9.265: Flights that never touch the arm switch (bench or simulated sessions) now save to flash via the link-dead fallback — Previous flights finally populate on receivers with an arming channel set.
v0.9.266: One-button polish: the No-transmitter-connected notice shows a single OK (OK and Cancel did the same thing).
v0.9.267: The no-transmitter notice now has exactly one button: Well of course!
v0.9.268: Saved flights are labelled with real date and time — the phone teaches the receiver the clock on every page visit, and flights saved before you connected are dated retroactively.
v0.9.269: Honest gap statistics: the receiver measures its own packet spacing (2 ms solo, 4 ms buddy-box) and counts only packets meaningfully LATE (default 5 ms or more, adjustable on the flight page) — and bills them only for the late part. The histogram now shows real anomalies, not every normal packet.
v0.9.270: Radio-swap count freezes at signal loss, exactly like the per-radio times — bench hunting while the transmitter is off is no longer billed to the flight.
v0.9.271: BLE quarantine for the black box: while a phone is connected over Bluetooth (or briefly around connect/disconnect), gaps and swaps are not billed to the RF link — the ESP32 BT radio desenses the nRF24s centimetres away, which never happens in real flight. Bench stats with the app attached now reflect the link, not the phone.
v0.9.272: Gap and swap statistics count ONLY when Bluetooth is fully off (fly mode) - nobody flies with Bluetooth on, so figures recorded with it running were never useful.
v0.9.273: Frame rate now reads the TRUE link rate from the measured packet spacing (matches the transmitter, ~500 Hz) instead of packets-divided-by-time; and a flight entered with the phone attached starts recording stats the moment the phone link drops.
v0.9.274: Fly now means true radio silence: the phone link is dropped too (it used to stay alive so fly mode could be cancelled from the app, but a live Bluetooth link desenses the RC radios). The way back is a power-cycle or landing auto-recovery.
v0.9.275: Three lodge-test refinements: the spacing estimator no longer lets missed-slot gaps inflate it (frame rate now agrees with the transmitter, ~500), transmitter power-off hesitations of ANY size are trimmed from the end of a flight record, and the post-Fly screen honestly says the Bluetooth link is closed instead of offering a button that cannot work.
v0.9.276: Frame rate tracks the true slot floor (retried packets no longer bias it - should now match the transmitter within a whisker) and the Bluetooth on/off quiet windows widen to 4 s so BT tail-end bursts cannot sneak one late packet into the record.
v0.9.277: Frame rate is now measured the V1 way: packets counted per second, exactly as the transmitter counts acknowledgements - the two ends finally use the same definition and must agree.
v0.9.278: Fly now zeroes the whole flight record 3 seconds later (Malcolm) - link stats AND the telemetry graph restart once the radios are truly quiet, so a flight begins at Fly, not at the bench.
v0.9.279: The battery guardian: at 3.5 V/cell the app shows a massive pulsing warning; at 3.3 V/cell - only if the channels have been dead-still for 2 minutes and the model is not armed or flying - the receiver saves the flight and deep-sleeps to spare the pack. A flying model always moves its channels, so sleep can never fire mid-air. Wake = power-cycle.
v0.9.280: Renaming the receiver over Bluetooth no longer strands you on a white page - the app shows a clear rebooting-as-NewName screen and tells you to reconnect from the scanner.
RXV2-0.9.281-exit-and-reload: After a rename the screen now says exactly what to do - exit and reload, the receiver reappears under its new name. Also fixed: the Android app was taking WiFi-flavoured wording everywhere (its Bluetooth disguise was not recognised).
RXV2-0.9.282-heli-wave: The Bluetooth-ready wave now shows on flight-controller models too (the disarmed FC passes cyclic to the swash, so you can see it) - with an extra guard: FC models only wave when no transmitter is live, so a mid-air reboot can never wiggle a flying machine.
RXV2-0.9.283-eight-flights: The black box now keeps the last EIGHT flights (was three) - a couple of bench tests can no longer push a real flight out of history. Updates still preserve all saved flights.
RXV2-0.9.284-flight-diary: The flight diary: keeps the last TWENTY flights; unarmed sessions under a minute are wiggle-checks and no longer saved at all; and updates now skip rewriting the web filesystem when it is unchanged (fingerprint match) - so saved flights survive every firmware-only update untouched and field updates get much faster. Background photo slimmed to make room.
RXV2-0.9.285-graph-scales: Flight-page polish from field review: the graph gains quarter-height gridlines and per-minute time marks (each trace still auto-scales to its own min-max shown in the key); the page title no longer hides behind the corner buttons; and a radio handover is now correctly billed to the flight (a 9-minute flight showed both radios busy yet zero swaps) - unbilled swaps leave a note in the events log saying why.
RXV2-0.9.286-landscape-graph: Turn the phone sideways on the flight page and the graph grows to fill most of the screen - landscape is reading mode, with a crisp high-resolution redraw on every rotation.
RXV2-0.9.287-y-scale: In landscape, every gridline now carries the actual VALUES - one number per trace, printed in that traces colour (each line has its own scale, so read the number that matches the colour). Also the corner buttons no longer sit on top of the cards in landscape.
RXV2-0.9.288-save-stall-quiet: Malcolm caught the receiver blaming the air for its own housekeeping: saving the flight at disarm stalls the loop (~1s with the 20-slot rotation) and an 808ms gap was billed exactly at arming-off. Saves now announce themselves and the statistics look away - self-inflicted stalls are never recorded as link quality.
RXV2-0.9.289-quiet-moment-save: Landing no longer makes the transmitter blink: the flight save now writes ONE ring slot instead of shuffling twenty files, and it waits for a provably quiet moment - disarmed with sticks still for two seconds (or transmitter off). A pilot flying an autorotation is never hands-still, so the save can never stall the link mid-air.
RXV2-0.9.290-ten-ms-doctrine: The 10ms doctrine: flight saves now trickle out a few hundred bytes per loop pass - no single pause the transmitter can even see (it logged the old save as a 250ms gap the receiver politely did not). And when WiFi is off with no phone attached and the link has been live 30 seconds, Bluetooth switches off too - nobody flies with Bluetooth on; it returns by itself after landing.
RXV2-0.9.291-flight-eraser: The flight diary gains an eraser: a Delete button appears when viewing any saved flight (never the live one) - tap twice to confirm, and a brief boring test vanishes to free its slot.
RXV2-0.9.292-govcfg-tracer: Detective work: the transmitter's global governor screen stays blank while the phone reads the same settings fine. This build adds breadcrumbs to the events log at every step of that path - open the screen on the transmitter once, and the log will point at the guilty stage.
RXV2-0.9.293-no-zero-latch: Case closed: the transmitter's global governor screen showed zeros because the receiver kept broadcasting empty parameter slots while the transmitter's request was still in flight - the screen latched the zeros and stopped listening a tenth of a second before the real values arrived. Now, like V1, those slots stay silent unless there is genuinely something to say.
RXV2-0.9.294-verified-writes: Trust, but verify: saving settings from the transmitter used to fire commands at the flight controller and hope - and on a busy wire the crucial save-to-memory command could vanish, quietly reverting your edit. Every write is now acknowledged, read back, compared and retried until confirmed; the governor reboot only fires once the save is proven. One press of Save now means exactly one save.
RXV2-0.9.295-honest-warnings: No more crying wolf: saving the global governor from the phone cleared its 'unsaved changes' flag only after the flight controller had rebooted and been re-read - leave the page during those ten seconds and it warned you the save was lost when it wasn't. The flag now clears the instant the save is confirmed in flash, and the after-reboot check patiently retries instead of declaring failure on one slow reply.
RXV2-0.9.296-dated-flights: Every flight now says when it happened: the Flight analysis card leads with the date and time (learned quietly from your phone's clock each time the app connects), not just the position in the list. Flights saved before the receiver ever knew the time say so honestly.
RXV2-0.9.297-tx-clock: The transmitter becomes the timekeeper: its battery-backed, GPS-synchronised clock now tells the receiver the time just after every connection - so flights get proper dates even on phone-free field days, and a battery swap no longer wipes the receiver's sense of time. The phone still teaches the timezone (remembered forever) and takes precedence when connected. Requires the matching transmitter update.
RXV2-0.9.298-clock-candour: The transmitter-clock feature now narrates itself: every time packet from the TX is logged with its fate - applied ('Clock set by TX'), outranked ('TX clock heard - phone rules', normal whenever the phone is connected), or rejected with the raw values. No more silent mysteries when testing at the bench.
RXV2-0.9.299-param-trace: Detective's notebook: the receiver now logs every kind of parameter packet the transmitter sends, once per power-on - so 'did the time packet even arrive?' is answered by a glance at the event log. Pairs with a transmitter update that re-sends its clock every minute instead of trusting one fragile moment at connect.
RXV2-0.9.300-clock-calibration: Version 300! The transmitter's clock turned out to show UTC plus six minutes of drift, not local time - never assume. The receiver now calibrates it against the phone whenever both are present (every bench session), remembers the offset, and applies it on phone-free field days. Flight stamps come out right no matter what the transmitter's clock face believes.
RXV2-0.9.301-clock-on-screen: The clock steps on stage: the Black box status card now shows the receiver's date and time and who taught it (phone or transmitter, with the calibration figure), and the current flight's card says when the session started - so you can see at a glance that the timekeeping is alive, not just trust the event log.
RXV2-0.9.302-phone-teaches-tx: The circle closes: whenever the receiver's clock came from a phone, it now offers that true time back to the transmitter over the radio link (ack item 37) - and the updated transmitter quietly corrects its own drifty clock from it. Most models never carry GPS, but every model meets a phone; now every phone connection keeps the whole fleet's clocks honest. Needs the matching transmitter update.
RXV2-0.9.303-help-catches-up: The help screens catch up with reality: flying needs no buttons (transmitter on first and the radios manage themselves - explained on the front page), the flight diary holds twenty dated flights with a delete button and landscape mode, and the Black box help explains the self-tending clocks. Written down so nobody has to remember - not even the author.
RXV2-0.9.304-field-telemetry: Field fix from today's three test flights: after landing away from home WiFi, the receiver kept the flight controller cut off during its ~2 minutes of hopeful WiFi retries - so the Black box showed 'no telemetry' with the battery plugged in. The flight-controller line now stays connected throughout, and the battery card fills in seconds at the field, just as it does at home.
RXV2-0.9.305-every-page-teaches-time: Every page now teaches the receiver the time, and the Black box page re-teaches it the moment it notices the clock is unset - so sitting on one screen through a receiver reboot no longer leaves it ignorant of the date until you happen to navigate. One shared, rate-limited helper replaces the per-page copies.
RXV2-0.9.306-tuning-notes: Malcolm's suggestion after an evening of governor tuning: when Rotorflight settings were edited from the transmitter during a session, the flight statistics now carry a friendly amber note explaining that the transmitter pauses briefly for each read or save - so the larger gaps and radio swaps it causes are expected, not a link problem. No more alarming numbers without context.
RXV2-0.9.307-seaworthy-lifeboat: A sad discovery and its fix: the lifeboat that carries saved flights across page updates was boarding passengers in the wrong order - under memory pressure it saved arbitrary old flights and lost the newest, which is how yesterday's first dated field flights drowned. It now boards newest-first, uses the board's big PSRAM when available (the whole 20-flight diary fits), and the event log honestly reports 'N of M flights aboard' at every crossing.
RXV2-0.9.308-flight-page-fix: Emergency repair: yesterday's tidy-up left one line on the Flight analysis page running before the shared library existed - the error silently killed the whole page, which is why it showed no flights at all despite the diary being intact. One line removed; every saved flight reappears.
RXV2-0.9.309-ask-and-receive: Ask and receive (Malcolm's idea): opening the flight list is itself proof the pilot is on the ground - so it now ends the save's polite waiting immediately, and while the write completes the selector says 'saving the last flight, a moment...' instead of leaving you wondering. The safety rules are untouched: saves still never run while armed.
RXV2-0.9.310-pardon-the-pause: Malcolm noticed the only >100ms gap in his transmitter's log was the flight being saved to flash just after motor-off - honest, but it polluted the averages. Now the receiver announces the pause before it happens ('pardon the next 3 seconds', ack item 38), and the updated transmitter excludes those gaps from every statistic, logging 'Gap excused (RX saving flight)' instead. The link's numbers now describe the link, and nothing else.
RXV2-0.9.311-pardoned-teardowns: Bench detective work with Malcolm solved the mystery 536ms field gap: switching the radios off (Fly now, or Bluetooth's silence-while-flying) stalls the processor ~0.7s - real, deliberate, and previously billed as a link gap. Now the receiver announces the pardon before any intentional radio shutdown (the transmitter excludes it by name), the shutdown waits politely for its announcement to arrive, and - the safety heart of it - automatic radio teardowns can never fire while the model is ARMED. Plus: the Bluetooth tail-wave announces a revival once, not twice.
RXV2-0.9.312-one-wave-per-landing: Refinement from the bench session: the spurious second tail-wave could arrive a minute or two after the first (the field's WiFi giving up on home and starting its hotspot re-announced Bluetooth), so the debounce is now keyed to the LANDING itself rather than any clock - one wave per landing, unlimited flights per day, and the WiFi machinery's internal restarts stay properly silent. Includes 0.9.311's pardoned teardowns: radio shutdowns announce themselves to the transmitter and can never fire while armed.
RXV2-0.9.313-steadfast-delete: The reluctant flight, explained: deleting several flights in quick succession shifted the list's numbering under the page, so a delete could aim at an already-empty slot and appear to do nothing. Deletions now target the flight's permanent storage slot, which never moves - every delete lands exactly where you pointed, however fast you prune.
RXV2-0.9.314-save-to-phone: Malcolm's suggestion made flesh: a 'Save session to phone' button on the Black box page (visible in the app) explicitly records everything - flights, graphs, events, Rotorflight settings - with a live count and a proud 'All saved!' at the end. The armchair review is now something you can deliberately pack in your pocket before switching off, not just hope the background recorder caught.
RXV2-0.9.315-solid-text: Solid, readable text everywhere: cards, banners, titles and messages now sit on solid backgrounds (no more translucency washing out in sunlight). Rotorflight settings are now saved and reviewed PER BANK (all 4 PID banks + 4 rate banks, transmitter off), offline edits remember their bank, and the Save-session button no longer appears while reviewing.
RXV2-0.9.316-progress-bar: Saving the session to the phone now shows a solid, readable progress panel with a real progress bar. Offline edits made in review are no longer discarded when you connect with the transmitter on — they are kept until sent (transmitter off) or overwritten by newer edits.
RXV2-0.9.317-honest-save: When reviewing offline in the app, the Rotorflight save buttons now tell the truth: 'Save to phone', with matching confirmations and '✓ Saved on the phone — ready to send at the next connection' messages (copy-to-profile too). The governor page no longer pretends to reboot a flight controller that isn't there.
RXV2-0.9.318-flight-list-fix: Fixes 'all my flights are gone': the flight LIST broke the moment flights gained real dates (a 64-byte line buffer truncated the JSON) — the flight data itself was always safe on the receiver. All saved flights reappear.
RXV2-0.9.319-fool-armour: Guard rails for busy fingers: the save-to-phone panel warns not to switch the transmitter on or the model off mid-save, and the apps now abort bank switching instantly (restoring the model's own banks) if the transmitter appears mid-save. Sending offline edits re-checks the transmitter at the moment you press Send, shows what to keep on/off, and NEVER loses edits if a step fails — they are kept for another try. Plus: the app now keeps a separate recorded session PER MODEL; connecting a different model no longer erases the previous one's.
RXV2-0.9.320-smooth-curves: The flight graph now draws real slopes instead of staircases: each sensor's discrete steps are turned back into the smooth curve the quantity actually followed. And when reviewing offline, the tuning pages now honestly say 'Loaded from the phone' / 'Reload from phone'.
RXV2-0.9.321-steady-hand: Graph refinement: a governed head speed now draws truly FLAT — small sensor jitter (a few rpm, hundredths of a volt) is treated as steadiness rather than continuous change, especially visible on short flights. Real changes still slope exactly as before.
RXV2-0.9.322-straight-slopes: Graph lines are now straight slopes with gently rounded corners instead of sweeping curves — sparse data no longer swoops like a sine wave.
RXV2-0.9.323-square-events: Graph: real events (motor on/off, battery plugged in) now draw square — the flat holds its full length and the change is steep at the moment it happened. Only gentle one-unit sensor steps are smoothed into slopes.
RXV2-0.9.324-current-lag-note: Flight-analysis help now explains why current seems to lag head speed on spool-up: the ESC smooths and reports current more slowly than RPM — the reporting lags, not the motor.
RXV2-0.9.325-gear-field-fix: The gear-ratio box no longer fights your typing — the page's background refresh was rewriting it mid-keystroke. Type, save, done.
RXV2-0.9.326-fast-lane-update: Updates take the fastest road automatically: when the receiver's own WiFi is connected, installs download at WiFi speed even when you're using the app over Bluetooth (30-90 s instead of minutes). Bluetooth streaming remains the automatic fallback at the field.
RXV2-0.9.327-no-silent-sbus: Fixes the mystery CRSF-to-SBUS reverts: quick bench sessions ending with a battery pull (transmitter still on) were counted as crash reboots, and the third one silently reset the protocol. The healthy-boot counter now clears even with the transmitter on (never while armed, gap pardoned), and crash recovery no longer rewrites your saved protocol at all - it just uses SBUS for that one boot.
RXV2-0.9.328-crsf-everywhere: CRSF is now the default in every corner: even a crash-recovery boot speaks CRSF (the fleet's language) instead of SBUS, so a rescued receiver still talks to its Rotorflight FC. Saved settings remain untouched by recovery.
RXV2-0.9.329-fc-cell-count: Battery cell count now comes from the flight controller itself (MSP battery state) instead of being guessed from voltage — a 12S pack at 45 V no longer masquerades as an 11S. The guess remains only as a fallback for models without an FC answer.
RXV2-0.9.330-even-cells: Cell-count guessing got wiser: packs above 4S only come in even counts (6S, 8S, 12S — never 11S), so the voltage fallback now rounds odd guesses up. The flight controller's own answer still wins when available.
RXV2-0.9.331-tuning-polish: Tuning pages polished: Save and Back now float at the bottom of the screen (no more scrolling); every save reads BACK from the flight controller and announces 'Written & verified!' right on the button; and the app's background recording now waits its turn so pages never show another bank's values. The update page also says up front whether an install will use WiFi (fast) or Bluetooth, and why.
RXV2-0.9.332-switch-model: New front-screen button in the app: 'Load another model' — drops back to the receiver list to pick a different craft, no more force-quitting the app to change models.
RXV2-0.9.333-fast-lane-banner: The front-page update banner now takes the WiFi fast lane too — the earlier fix only covered the Check-for-Update page, so banner installs still streamed over Bluetooth even with the receiver on WiFi.
RXV2-0.9.334-keyboard-buttons: The floating Save/Back bar now rides up above the on-screen keyboard while you edit a value, instead of sinking behind it.
RXV2-0.9.335-bank-assert: Every save now re-selects its own bank at the exact moment of writing — no possibility of values landing in a different bank, no matter what else is talking to the flight controller. Combined with read-back verification, saves are now bank-proof end to end.
RXV2-0.9.336-phone-restore: The confused pilot's parachute: 'Restore settings from phone' on the Rotorflight page writes back EVERY recorded setting — PIDs, advanced PIDs, rates and governor, all four banks — from the app's session recording, even if no backup was ever made. Transmitter must be off; every item is verified by read-back.
RXV2-0.9.337-named-verify: Phone-restore polish: each item now gets a second attempt if a radio hiccup interrupts it, and anything that still fails to verify is named ('rates bank 2') instead of counted — so you know exactly what to check.
RXV2-0.9.338-maxvel-editable: Rates page: Max Vel is now editable (it shares one stored value with Rate — editing either keeps the other in step, matching the official Configurator).
RXV2-0.9.339-one-backup-system: One backup system: the Rotorflight page now carries 'Back up settings to phone' and 'Restore settings from phone' side by side (the phone recording covers every bank, verified on restore). The old receiver-side named-backups page is retired.
RXV2-0.9.340-backup-help: Help screens now spell out that backing up to the phone captures ALL the Black box data (every saved flight and the event log) as well as every bank's Rotorflight settings — the phone becomes a complete backup of the model.
RXV2-0.9.341-fewer-twitches: The little swashplate twitch during bank changes and saves is the flight controller pausing to write its memory (the official Configurator does it too) — harmless, now explained in the help. The app also skips unnecessary bank changes during backup and restore, so it happens less.
RXV2-0.9.342-proven-tune-nudge: The receiver now notices when a tune has PROVEN itself: after Rotorflight edits followed by six or more flights with no further changes, the app's front page gently suggests backing the tune up to the phone — once per tune, dismissable. Works across battery cycles and counts transmitter edits too.
RXV2-0.9.343-telem-watchdog: Chasing the field telemetry dropout: the event log now records exactly WHEN flight-controller telemetry stops and when it resumes (with durations), and the battery-cell-count query stops pestering flight controllers that never answer it.
RXV2-0.9.344-event-afterlife: Chasing the Bluetooth-dead-after-landing bug: the event log now SURVIVES reboots (persisted to flash at safe moments, previous boot readable afterwards and captured by session saves), and a watchdog keeps re-trying the post-landing Bluetooth revival every 30 s instead of leaving you to reboot.
RXV2-0.9.345-instant-check: The manual Check-for-Update page is now as instant as the automatic prompt: inside the app it reads the release list with the PHONE's internet (like the front-page banner always did) instead of asking the receiver to fetch web pages over its own WiFi — which was slow at best and impossible with the transmitter on.
RXV2-0.9.346-short-caption: Shorter, calmer graph caption: 'Each line auto-scaled to its own range (min-max in the key).' The tutorial sentence moved out of the way.
RXV2-0.9.347-rename-returns: After renaming a receiver (or finishing first-run setup) in the app, you're taken straight back to the model list, where it reappears under its new name — no more force-quitting to reconnect.
RXV2-0.9.348-no-stuck-waits: No more stuck 'waiting for it to come back' screens: after an install the app reconnects via a fresh Bluetooth discovery (the reliable path), and if reconnection still hasn't happened ~100 s after the reboot, both install screens return you to the model list to reconnect there — the update itself is already safely installed.
RXV2-0.9.349-one-rename: One way to rename: the duplicate rename card on the WiFi page (which misbehaved over Bluetooth) is retired — tap the model name on the front screen instead.
RXV2-0.9.350-deterministic-install: The manual install now uses exactly the strategy that made the automatic prompt reliable: fire the install, ignore its doomed reply, and judge only by the receiver's version changing — with a visible seconds counter and a guaranteed return to the model list if Bluetooth hasn't re-linked by ~100 s (the update is installed either way). No stuck screens, by construction.
RXV2-0.9.351-install-post-fires: Fixes the stuck manual-install screen for real: a scope bug meant the install command was never actually sent to the receiver — the page then waited forever for an update that never started. The command now fires (proven by an automated page test), the seconds counter runs, and the page returns you to the model list if Bluetooth hasn't re-linked by ~100 s.
RXV2-0.9.352-reinstall-aware: Reinstalling the SAME version no longer confuses the install screen: success is now judged by the receiver going quiet (flashing) and coming back on the target version, which works for updates and reinstalls alike. Both paths proven by automated page tests.
RXV2-0.9.353-install-progress-bar: The manual install screen now shows a moving progress bar (like the front-page update prompt) with a phase note that switches to 'flashing + rebooting' when the receiver goes quiet — no more bare seconds counter during the wait.
RXV2-0.9.354-honest-flight-notes: Two flight-screen fixes from Black Thunder II's first flights: the yellow note now says Rotorflight screens were VIEWED (or edited) from the transmitter — just browsing screens fires parameter reads, so it no longer claims edits you never made. And the Black box status keeps showing the battery's LAST-KNOWN voltage (greyed, with its age) after the model powers down — exactly when you check the packs landed at 3.80 V/cell — instead of going blank.
RXV2-0.9.355-travel-extents: NEW: 'Travel extents' screen in the Rotorflight menu — born at the field when Black Thunder II's first hover showed nowhere near enough collective pitch. Edit the collective pitch limit, cyclic pitch limit, total swash limit, swashplate trims and tail travel (Rotorflight 2.3 mixer limits) right from the phone. Changes apply immediately (no reboot), are saved to the flight controller's memory, and are verified by read-back. Always check new extents on the bench before flying.
RXV2-0.9.356-travel-extents-2: Travel extents fixes: mixer inputs are now read one at a time (the bulk read could never fit through the radio link, which is why the first version failed to load), and the status message is sticky at the top of the screen so it stays visible next to the Reload/Save buttons.
RXV2-0.9.357-travel-gains: Travel extents gains: new 'Calibration (gains)' card with collective and cyclic gain (%) — the scale that makes commanded degrees equal REAL measured degrees. Malcolm's first live read showed the FC commanding 14 deg while the blades reached only 5-7: raise the gain by the measured ratio (direction is always preserved — only the amount changes), use collective trim to centre a non-zero mid-stick, then re-measure.
RXV2-0.9.358-geo-correction: Travel extents: new Geo correction field — Rotorflight's knob for unequal positive vs negative collective (Black Thunder II read +12.6 up but -14.9 down after gain calibration). Step it one way, re-measure, reverse if the gap widens; direction of every control is still preserved.
RXV2-0.9.359-plain-names: Plainer words on Travel extents (Malcolm: Rotorflight's own names make it impenetrable — 'geo correction' sounds like GPS!): the field is now 'Collective up/down balance', with a note giving Rotorflight's name for cross-reference with their docs.
RXV2-0.9.360-plain-english: Plain English across ALL Rotorflight screens (Malcolm: brilliant technicians were frequently simply not taught good English!). Every cryptic label now says what it does, with Rotorflight's own term kept in brackets for cross-reference: 'Hold cyclic true in pirouettes (piro comp)', 'Roll wind-up relief (I-term relax cutoff)', 'Stick sharpening (setpoint boost gain)', 'Tail-torque assist strength (TTA gain)', 'Throttle anticipation (feed-forward weights)', 'Quick-restart time (recovery time)', and friends — 45 labels in all.
RXV2-0.9.361-bench-measure: Bench measure on Travel extents: hold the swash at an exact angle with the gyros bypassed (Rotorflight's mixer override) so a pitch gauge can calibrate CYCLIC gain from the phone — no laptop. Pick Roll/Pitch/Collective and an angle, 'Hold this angle', measure the PEAK reading while rotating the head, then gain = current x commanded/peak. Guarded: refuses while armed, the FC refuses to arm while held, released on leaving the page and by a 5-minute auto-release. A step toward the full phone setup wizard.
RXV2-0.9.362-bench-zeroed: Bench measure fix (Malcolm's own diagnosis, first try: 8 deg roll measured -24!): while holding one axis, the OTHER swash axes are now held at ZERO instead of following the live mixer — with no transmitter, collective was sitting at full-low underneath the measurement. A pure 8 deg roll now measures as just that.
RXV2-0.9.363-bench-official: Verified against the Rotorflight source: the Bench measure IS Rotorflight's own official calibration method (their configurator sends the identical command). Collective removed from the bench axis picker — on this fleet it is calibrated the direct full-stick way, because the transmitter channel span is part of that story. Swash trims relabelled to % (Rotorflight's actual unit — they were mislabelled degrees).
RXV2-0.9.364-bench-polish: Travel extents polish: tail travel renamed to 'nose left / nose right' (a tail swinging left sends the NOSE right — plain left/right labels mislead), and the bench buttons grey out when meaningless: Hold is disabled while that exact hold is already active, Release is disabled when nothing is held.
RXV2-0.9.365-stick-frame-tail: Tail travel is now named by the RUDDER STICK — 'stick left / stick right' (Malcolm's suggestion), bound to the direction each field really limits on these transmitters as verified on the bench. Stick-left listed first, as a hand would expect.
RXV2-0.9.366-keyboard-aware-save: The bottom Save/Back bar now rides up above the iOS keyboard instead of hiding underneath it (Malcolm: 'I have to scroll to find Save to Flight Controller'). Works on every tuning page - the bar follows the visual viewport whenever a number field opens the keyboard.
RXV2-0.9.367-saved-flash: Travel extents: the Save button itself briefly flashes 'Saved!' after a successful, verified save - same friendly confirmation the governor pages have.
RXV2-0.9.368-keyboard-exact: Save bar now clears the keyboard exactly: the keyboard swallows the home-indicator safe area but the bar's padding still reserved it, leaving the buttons half-hidden - reclaimed while raised.
RXV2-0.9.369-badge-dot: The Bluetooth/WiFi pill shrinks to a small dot - it was covering page content, and by now everyone knows how they're connected. In the app the dot is still the disconnect button: tap it, confirm.
RXV2-0.9.370-blue-tooth: The Bluetooth badge is now a literal blue TOOTH (Malcolm's pun, irresistible) - a little molar on the blue dot, still the tap-to-disconnect button.
RXV2-0.9.371-genmoji-tooth: The Bluetooth badge is now Malcolm's own Genmoji: a glossy blue tooth with signal waves on the enamel, drawn on his iPhone. Still tap-to-disconnect.
RXV2-0.9.406-arm-cycle: Automatic fly mode, full cycle: radios switch OFF by themselves 3 s after ARMING (on the ground, during spool-up - never mid-air) and back ON when you DISARM. Only WiFi/Bluetooth are touched; the RC link and flight-controller output never stop. With an arming channel set, the front-page Fly now button hides itself - it is no longer needed (models without arming keep it).
RXV2-0.9.407-arm-self-taught: Rotorflight takes over Fly now completely: the receiver reads the ARM switch channel straight from the flight controller (MSP mode ranges) - no setup needed. Fly now then hides itself and the arming switch does it all: arm = radios off (3 s, on the ground), disarm = radios back. A manually set arming channel still wins; non-Rotorflight models are unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.408-new-heli: The NEW HELICOPTER wizard begins: a step-by-step from-scratch setup checklist (blades off!) plus the new First-time basics page - level calibration (accelerometer), governor/telemetry/ESC-sensor features, ESC protocol + motor poles + gear ratios, ESC telemetry brand, battery cells/capacity/voltage sources, and one-tap standard channel order (AERCT123). All writes verified by read-back; restart-to-apply handled in-page.
RXV2-0.9.409-fw-note: New-helicopter checklist gains step 1: a note that a fresh flight controller already has Rotorflight on it (fine to fly), and that installing the very latest firmware first is a one-time USB job with the Rotorflight Configurator on a computer - flashing cannot be done from the phone. A desktop wizard that flashes too is planned.
RXV2-0.9.410-fleet-ticks: New-helicopter checklist is now PER MODEL: ticks are keyed by the receiver's name, so a whole fleet of new helicopters each starts its own fresh checklist ('Setting up: <name>' shown at the top).
RXV2-0.9.411-tuning-wizard: Second wizard: TUNING - the after-the-build field checklist, in the order that works: back up first, mechanics check in the hover, governor, tail, cyclic, rates/expo to taste, fine touches, prove Rescue up high, back up the proven tune. One change per flight; ticks per model, like the New-helicopter checklist.
RXV2-0.9.412-tx-first: Transmitter first! New wizard step + page: set the model up on your transmitter, then tell the wizard which channel is which - or tap Detect and wiggle each control (the receiver spots the moving channel). Saving writes the flight controller's channel order (rcmap) and puts Arm & Rescue on your chosen switches (Modes, 1600-2100us), all verified by read-back. Your layout is remembered as the default for the next helicopter.
RXV2-0.9.413-mounting: First-time basics gains 'Which way round is it mounted?' - the only two real Nexus positions: connections to the FRONT (standard) or to the BACK (yaw 180, board_align_yaw). Set FIRST, above level calibration, since level depends on it; applies after the in-page FC restart. Odd angles are reported as custom (configurator territory). Verified writes as always.
RXV2-0.9.414-tidy-hub: The Rotorflight page, tidied into three groups now that it has grown: STEP-BY-STEP GUIDES (New helicopter, Tuning), INDIVIDUAL SETTINGS (transmitter channels through PIDs, roughly in setup order), and BACKUP & RESTORE with its own heading. Nothing moved pages - just a calmer front door.
RXV2-0.9.415-three-doors: The Rotorflight page is now just three doors (Malcolm's words): WIZARDS (new helicopter, tuning), A LA CARTE (straight to any single setting), and BACKUP & RESTORE on its own page. Every page is where it was - only the front door changed.
RXV2-0.9.416-wizard-steps: Transmitter channels and First-time basics moved to the Wizards page where they belong - they are the build wizard's two big steps, listed there for a straight jump. A la carte now holds only the individual tuning/setup pages.
RXV2-0.9.417-more-functions: Transmitter channels grows 'Add another function' - black box, beeper, self-level, governor overrides, user switches and more, each detectable by wiggle and written as a verified switch range. Two functions may share one switch; sticks and Arm may never be shared. The Wizards menu is now just the two guides - Transmitter channels and First-time basics live inside the New-helicopter wizard as its steps 3 and 4.
RXV2-0.9.418-complete-menu: A la carte is now the COMPLETE catalogue: Transmitter channels and First-time basics appear there too, so everything the wizards walk through can also be reached on its own. The Wizards menu stays clean with just the two guides.
RXV2-0.9.419-esc-words: Clearer ESC wording after Malcolm went looking for Scorpion under ESC signal: the SIGNAL row now says heli ESCs (Scorpion, Kontronik, YGE, Hobbywing) use Normal PWM and DShot is for drone-style ESCs; the TELEMETRY row now says that is where the brand goes.
RXV2-0.9.420-named-switches: Added functions on Transmitter channels are now tidy stacked cards that fit the phone screen (the old row overflowed sideways), and each can be given YOUR OWN NAME - a User switch might really be 'Lower undercarriage'. The name lives in the app; the flight controller sees the function.
RXV2-0.9.421-settled-rows: Added functions now settle in: name one (e.g. 'Sally'), hit return, and the row collapses to look exactly like the fixed rows above - name on the left, channel, live value, Detect. Tap the name to edit it again. New rows open in editing form with the keyboard ready.
RXV2-0.9.422-erasable: Added functions can now be deleted cleanly: the X on each row (after a confirm) removes it AND clears its switch range from the flight controller if it had been saved - experiments and mistakes leave no trace. Only the exact function-on-that-switch is cleared; everything else is untouched.
RXV2-0.9.423-no-collisions: Two field-driven fixes on Transmitter channels: (1) taken channels are simply not offered in the other dropdowns any more (switch functions may still share with each other - only sticks and Arm are exclusive); (2) the Rescue switch can be removed entirely (X sets None and clears any saved rescue from the flight controller - some models just don't have one), and saving with Rescue=None also wipes a stale saved rescue.
RXV2-0.9.424-strict-channels: Strictly one channel per function now: taken channels vanish from every other dropdown (no sharing at all), existing double-bookings are repaired on load (the later claimant resets to 'Choose...', keeping its name), and the stick labels lose their bracketed words - just Aileron, Elevator, Collective, Rudder, Throttle.
RXV2-0.9.425-arming-plain: 'Arming switch' is now simply 'Arming' - it is a channel, not necessarily a switch: some radios drive it from a safety switch or mix among other functions. (Malcolm's precision, gladly accepted.)
RXV2-0.9.426-rescue-plain: 'Rescue switch' is now simply 'Rescue', for the same reason as Arming: it is a channel, and what drives it is the radio's business.
RXV2-0.9.427-steady-front: No more front-screen shuffle: the app remembers the last known layout (Fly now hidden? Rotorflight present, and which version?) and paints it instantly at launch, before the receiver has even answered. The live state then only repaints if something actually changed - so on a Rotorflight model the right buttons are simply there from the first frame.
RXV2-0.9.428-fewer-words: Fewer words look clearer (Malcolm's doctrine, applied to the front screen): the automatic-fly-mode note line is gone (Receiver settings explains it), 'Bind' stands alone, 'Rotorflight config' drops the version number (it lives on the Rotorflight page), and 'Setup' loses its trailing list.
RXV2-0.9.429-wire-step: Wizard's 'Wire it up & first contact' step no longer has an Open button that led oddly back to the menu - it is a check, not a page: proof of life is the Rotorflight config button appearing on the front screen by itself.
RXV2-0.9.430-autofly-locked: SAFETY (after the 2026-08-24 crash): with Rotorflight present, automatic fly mode is FORCED ON and cannot be switched off - flying with the config link alive lets a blocking config request starve the CRSF stream, which Rotorflight reads as signal loss and cuts the motor. The Receiver-settings switch shows a lock; non-Rotorflight models keep the choice.
RXV2-0.9.431-armed-lockout: Completing the crash response: the moment the model is ARMED with a live transmitter, ALL configuration traffic to the flight controller is refused instantly ('ARMED - configuration is locked in flight. Disarm first.') - closing the 3-second window before auto fly mode kills the radios, and every other path. The stall-starves-CRSF-and-the-motor-cuts mechanism is now impossible at both ends.
RXV2-0.9.432-armed-banner: The loud goodbye: the moment arming comes on, every app page shows a full-screen red banner - 'ARMED! WiFi & Bluetooth are switching OFF for flying. The app disconnects in 3 seconds. Disarm the model to get it back.' The banner survives the disconnection (that IS the message) and clears when the link returns disarmed. Even the most enthusiastic, absent-minded pilot will notice.
RXV2-0.9.433-clocked-events: Two from Malcolm's bench log: (1) BUG FIX - with an arming channel known, the old 'link live 30s = flying' rule fought the new disarm revival, flapping the radios every 5 seconds on the bench with the transmitter on; ARMED is now the only definition of flying on such models (the old rule remains for models without arming). (2) The event log now shows the TIME OF DAY for every event once a phone has taught the receiver the clock - retroactively for events logged before the sync; time-since-boot before that.
RXV2-0.9.434-nudge-manners: The back-up-your-tune reminder now has manners: completing a backup (from either the Backup page or Black box) signs off the current tune generation, so the banner goes away and STAYS away until a setting actually changes - then it returns after six unchanged flights, exactly as before.
RXV2-0.9.435-pulse-spool: Malcolm's 'manual PWM' idea for neXt spool-up, built: PULSE MODE on the spool-up card - while spooling, the motor channel blips between full off and full on with a rising on-share (period adjustable, try 250 ms), so the sim's own rotor inertia averages it into a genuine head-speed climb even though neXt treats the motor as a pure switch. Two-speed bailout, torque stab and all existing behaviour unchanged; pulse off = exactly the old ramp.
RXV2-0.9.436-rf-never-forgotten: Three field reports from Malcolm's test day: (1) the Rotorflight options can no longer be forgotten - once Rotorflight is seen it STAYS seen (latched in the receiver for the whole boot, and remembered per model in the app) so detection flickers never hide the button; (2) the app's demo now carries full servo/rescue/switches/first-time data (no more 'undefined servos'); (3) the wave-test message explains that on a Rotorflight heli a rudder wave is invisible (yaw is a rate command the FC ignores while disarmed) - use ch1 aileron.
RXV2-0.9.437-lean-wizard: The wizards on a diet (Malcolm: easier to follow, dyslexia-friendly): every checklist step and intro is now one short action-first line - New helicopter, Tuning, First-time basics, Transmitter channels. All the detail still lives behind each page's ? button.
RXV2-0.9.438-visible-text: Readability pass (Malcolm's suggestions): the Back button is now bright green - findable at a glance instead of blending into the meadow; and every loose line of text sits on its own solid panel, no more faint words straight on the background photo.
RXV2-0.9.439-wiring-page: New Wiring page inside the New-helicopter wizard (Malcolm's spec): every plug on one line - S1 = the front-or-back servo then clockwise round the swash, tail on S4, ESC throttle lead, the one-wire telemetry to TLM, the RPM wire if your ESC has one, and the receiver's UART (CRSF). Head speed must arrive by telemetry or RPM wire, or the governor has nothing to govern.
RXV2-0.9.440-rx-port: Wiring page: which UART, answered - use the port labelled for the receiver (ELRS/RX), pre-configured for CRSF out of the box, nothing to declare. Any other UART is a chicken-and-egg that needs one configurator visit on USB.
RXV2-0.9.441-default-port: Wiring page: the port rule stated plainly - plug into the default receiver port (ELRS/RX) and it just works; any other port needs one configurator visit first.
RXV2-0.9.442-fw-recommended: Wizard step 1 is now 'Firmware update (recommended)' - update via the computer Configurator before you begin (new boards do fly as delivered).
RXV2-0.9.443-model-memory: Wizard step 3: 'Create a new model memory on your transmitter' - the proper term.
RXV2-0.9.444-imu-first: First-time basics reordered per Malcolm: 'Calibrate the flight controller' (IMU) is now the FIRST card - best done flat on a desk before the board goes in (the helicopter may not sit level), and front-or-back mounting does not affect it (the old 'set mounting first' note was wrong for flat boards). Wizard step 4 renamed to match.
RXV2-0.9.445-plain-features: First-time basics: the Features card now simply says 'Tick the functions you plan to use'; the receiver-link row is gone (it goes without saying - and the save still quietly keeps it on).
RXV2-0.9.446-help-sync: Help text matches the new Features wording (receiver reference gone there too).
RXV2-0.9.447-no-preset-map: Channel order no longer offers a 'standard' preset - it links straight to Transmitter channels, where each channel is chosen (or detected) properly.
RXV2-0.9.448-fc-wake: Wake a brand-new flight controller (Malcolm's first real Nexus X setup): factory boards ship with telemetry OFF and sit silent - undiscoverable. The Wiring page now offers (and has a button for) a one-tap Wake: the receiver blind-writes telemetry ON + save + restart over CRSF (the board listens even when mute). Protected: refused whenever a flight controller is already talking, so it can never touch a configured model.
RXV2-0.9.449-honest-first-contact: First-contact truth (tested live on the Goblin770's Nexus X): a factory-mute flight controller ignores incoming CRSF commands too, so it cannot be woken from the receiver side. The Wiring page now says the honest thing: one one-time computer step (Configurator - enable Telemetry - Save, it restarts) and the phone does everything after.
RXV2-0.9.450-computer-session-first: Wizard step 1 is now the one-time computer session, right at the top: turn Telemetry ON and set the serial input to the UART you are using (Save restarts the board); update firmware too while you're there. Everything after is phone-only.
RXV2-0.9.451-before-you-start: New 'Before you start' page (Malcolm's wording): the one USB session per new helicopter, as three numbered cards - update the firmware; check the serial port on the Configuration tab matches where the receiver is plugged; enable Telemetry on the Receiver tab then Save & Reboot (bottom right). Wizard step 1 opens it.
RXV2-0.9.452-tidy-wiring: Wiring page tidied: the brand-new-board card is gone - that story now lives on the Before-you-start page (wizard step 1).
RXV2-0.9.453-esc-port-truth: Before-you-start gains task 4 (found on the first real build): ESC telemetry cannot be fully enabled from the phone - the Ports tab must name which UART the ESC's data wire uses. The First-time basics tick now says so too.
RXV2-0.9.454-restart-to-apply: ESC telemetry verdict (proven live: 40.0C flowing on the Goblin770): the wizard could do it all along - features simply apply at BOOT. Saving features now offers the flight-controller restart on the spot, and Before-you-start is back to its three honest tasks (the Ports-tab task was a wrong diagnosis, withdrawn).
RXV2-0.9.455-wizard-logo: The wizard has a face: Malcolm's wizard-with-helicopter logo heads the Wizards hub and the New-helicopter checklist. Under the hood: three.js now lives gzipped on the receiver (668 KB to 166 KB) - room for many more pages.
RXV2-0.9.456-bank-rate-switches: Bank (PID profile) and Rates selectors, 4 positions each, from the phone: pick their channels on Transmitter channels (they may share one channel), Save writes them as Rotorflight adjustment ranges (proven live on the Goblin770 - top position = bank 4); the Switches page shows four blue zones with the live red marker AND the flight controller's own answer ('Flight controller: Bank 3') as you flip.
RXV2-0.9.457-jumbo-msp: Big flight-controller replies now arrive whole: MSP jumbo frames (0xFF + 16-bit length) reassembled into 640-byte buffers - the 588-byte adjustment table (bank/rates selectors) can be read back and verified, not just written.
RXV2-0.9.458-portable-backups: Backups travel (Malcolm's idea): Share backup file hands the whole setup to the phone's share sheet - email or AirDrop it to another phone, or to a friend with the same helicopter; Import a backup file adopts it as the model's restore point, then Restore writes it. The file carries everything, including the bank/rates switch selectors the flight controller cannot read back (now declared to the app when saved, restored verbatim). Needs app 3.21 / 3.13.
RXV2-0.9.459-one-bar: Bank and Rates rows on Transmitter channels now carry ONE bar divided into four sections (Malcolm: Rotorflight's three-bar adjustments are baffling) with the live red line and the current section lit green.
RXV2-0.9.460-six-sections: Bank & Rates selectors, refined (Malcolm): the bar now shows the live red tick with its microsecond value; the junctions between sections can be DRAGGED to resize them; and there are six sections (Rotorflight's six profiles) - sections 5 and 6 start zero-width at the top, drag them open if you need them. Under the hood each section is its own adjustment ('inside this section, profile = N'), so any widths are honoured exactly.
RXV2-0.9.461-tick-fix: Selector bars: the live red tick now actually shows (a display bug hid it); bigger junction handles that claim the touch so iOS can't turn a drag into a scroll.
RXV2-0.9.462-six-even: Selector bars start with all SIX sections evenly spaced (Malcolm: you then see the possibility and drag away the ones you don't need).
RXV2-0.9.463-selector-help: Transmitter channels: footer and help explain the Bank/Rates selector bars (sections, dragging, sharing a channel, why the app remembers them). Backup files are now dated.
RXV2-0.9.464-esc-setup: New wizard step 3, 'ESC setup (its own app)' (Malcolm): the six things the flight controller CANNOT set and the ESC's own programmer must - governor off/external (one governor only), throttle range 1000-2000, telemetry ON with the matching protocol, soft start short, BEC voltage for the servos, timing/brake + pole count.
RXV2-0.9.465-unstick-handles: Selector bars: junctions pushed together (e.g. to the far right) can be dragged apart again - a leftward drag takes the leftmost of the stack, rightward the rightmost.
RXV2-0.9.466-tribunus-tip: ESC page help: Scorpion Tribunus only accepts Sproto in its first seconds after power-up (click Connect, then plug the battery); a firmware update resets it to defaults - re-check governor, telemetry and throttle range.
RXV2-0.9.467-esc-calibration: ESC throttle calibration FROM THE PHONE (Malcolm's ask): the ESC page holds the motor channel at full throttle (renewed every half second, lapses by itself a second after the phone stops), you plug the battery, the ESC beeps, tap to drop to minimum, beeps again, done - the configurator's Motors-tab procedure without the computer. Guards: transmitter must be off, model disarmed, blades-off confirmation.
RXV2-0.9.468-plug-battery: ESC calibration (proven on a Tribunus!): the 'NOW PLUG THE FLIGHT BATTERY' instruction is a big orange banner - the one thing you must not miss.
RXV2-0.9.469-selectors-visible: Switches page: the Bank & Rates selectors card is always present - it says 'not set up yet' with a link to Transmitter channels until a Save has recorded them, then shows the bars and the flight controller's live answer.
RXV2-0.9.470-one-button-cal: ESC throttle calibration is now ONE big button whose words change with the stage (Start - PLUG THE BATTERY, wait for beeps, tap - WAIT FOR CONFIRMATION BEEPS, tap - CALIBRATED, unplug). No abort button: unplugging the battery is the abort, and the throttle hold lapses by itself.
RXV2-0.9.471-selectors-local: Switches page shows the Bank & Rates bars from this phone's choices even before a Save (marked as such), and the heading no longer runs together. Transmitter channels remembers its defaults.
RXV2-0.9.472-edit-selectors: Switches page: the Bank & Rates selectors are editable in place - channel picker, draggable section junctions, Save writes them to the flight controller (one truth shared with Transmitter channels).
RXV2-0.9.473-selectors-bite: Bank/Rates selectors now actually switch profiles: Rotorflight silently ignores a mapped adjustment whose min equals max, so each section is now written as N..N+1 with its mapping window centred on the section - the whole section lands on N. Re-save the selectors (Switches or Transmitter channels page) and flip the switch.
RXV2-0.9.474-selectors-verified: Selector maths verified against Rotorflight's own formula for even, quarter, uneven and two-section layouts (zero mismatches over the whole switch travel); sections near the top of travel use a mirrored window so nothing is lost at 2125. Re-save the selectors once.
RXV2-0.9.475-aux-off-by-one: IMPORTANT: switch channels were written ONE channel high to the flight controller. Rotorflight has five control channels (collective included), so its AUX1 is channel 6 - the pages used the channel-5 convention, so Arm, Rescue, added functions AND the bank/rates selectors all landed one channel above where you chose. Fixed on Switches and Transmitter channels. RE-SAVE on Transmitter channels once, then confirm with the live marker.
RXV2-0.9.476-one-adjustment: Selectors rebuilt on Rotorflight's own model: ONE adjustment per selector, equal sections between two draggable END points, with a positions count (2-6). Why: each Rotorflight adjustment remembers its last value and only fires when that changes, so per-section adjustments jam on re-entry (the 'stuck on profile 4'). Re-save once; drag the ends to your switch's lowest and highest positions.
RXV2-0.9.477-bar-scale-fix: Transmitter channels: the selector bars draw again (a missing scale constant crashed the Bank row and hid the Rates row).
RXV2-0.9.478-configurator-note: Selector cards and help now say where to find them in the configurator: Adjustments rows 31 (Bank) and 37 (Rates) - scroll a long way down.
RXV2-0.9.480-telemetry-sensors-fixed: 'Telemetry to the transmitter' in First-time basics: seven plain-English toggles (Flight mode, Battery, Head speed, Temperature, Attitude, Altitude, GPS) written into Rotorflight's sensor list, everything else preserved; Save verifies by read-back and offers the required restart. (Replaces 0.9.479, which mis-read the reply by one byte.)
RXV2-0.9.481-swash-copy: Servos: 'Copy to servos 2 & 3 & save' on servo 1 (Malcolm) - copies travel, throw, rate, slow-motion and geometry to the other swash servos in one tap; each keeps its own centre (mechanical levelling) and its own Reversed flag (mounting).
RXV2-0.9.483-control-sense: Travel extents gains a Control sense area (Malcolm): tick to reverse Aileron, Elevator or Collective - one control at a time, no negative numbers, servos untouched; applies on Save, no reboot.
RXV2-0.9.484-floating-back: A floating back arrow now sits beside the home button on every sub-page - one level up without scrolling; the old bottom 'Back to ...' buttons are gone.
RXV2-0.9.485-buttons-restored: Front screen's Rotorflight and Black box buttons are back (the floating-back change had hidden them by mistake); only genuine 'Back to ...' buttons are now hidden.
RXV2-0.9.486-one-true-back: Model-name chip fits again (width only narrows on pages with the back arrow); every page's embedded back button removed - the floating arrow now knows its own destination.
RXV2-0.9.487-simpler-switches: Switch cards on the Switches page lose the two microsecond number boxes - just the bar, the draggable ends and the live red tick.
RXV2-0.9.488-stateful-zones: Switch-card zone edges now live purely in memory - the number boxes are gone completely, not just hidden (less complexity down the road).
RXV2-0.9.489-tx-on-note: Switches and Transmitter-channels pages now remind you to have the transmitter ON - the live red tick needs it.
RXV2-0.9.490-uniform-switch-cards: Bank and Rates selector cards now share the exact layout of the other switch cards - same labelled pickers, bar and Save.
RXV2-0.9.491-arm-stays: The Arm switch card no longer offers Remove - Rotorflight requires an arm switch.
RXV2-0.9.492-title-fits: Page titles on back-arrow pages sit below the button row at full width - no more 'Switch / es' squeeze.
