RXV2-0.9.493-rescue-bar: Transmitter channels: Rescue gets the same blue bar as Bank/Rates showing its OFF and ON zones (drag the ends; ON above the middle); 'Bank (PID profile)' renamed 'Bank (Profile)'.
RXV2-0.9.494-arm-bar: Arming gets the same OFF/ON bar as Rescue (you can now SEE when the threshold is crossed); Rates carries a note that sharing Bank's channel is fine and popular.
RXV2-0.9.495-one-divider: Arming and Rescue bars: the useless end blobs are gone - ONE draggable divider sits on the OFF/ON threshold.
RXV2-0.9.496-no-end-blobs: Bank/Rates bars on both screens lose their end blobs - the travel is pinned to CRSF's known 988-2012 us, so there was nothing to drag.
RXV2-0.9.497-selectors-stay: Bank and Rates rows lose their delete (x) button - choosing None in the channel picker already covers the rare case; Rescue keeps its x.
RXV2-0.9.498-governor-why: ESC page now explains WHY Rotorflight's governor wins: it feeds throttle the instant collective demands it, before head speed sags - an ESC governor only reacts after the RPM drop.
RXV2-0.9.499-gear-in-wizard: Gear ratio moves into the Rotorflight area: editable card in the wizard's ESC step, its own page in A la carte (with live head speed), removed from Receiver settings.
RXV2-0.9.500-gear-mentions-gone: Setup-page button and help texts no longer mention gear ratio (it lives in the Rotorflight area now); dead gear code removed from Diagnostics.
RXV2-0.9.501-calibrate-first: Flight-controller calibration is now wizard step 2 with its own page (on the desk, before mounting) and an A-la-carte entry; also fixes the 'Can't find variable: LDRC' race on First-time basics.
RXV2-0.9.502-computer-notes: Step 1 notes the receiver need not be connected and that the post-flash 'calibration needed' warning can be ignored (or calibrate right there); step 2 opens with 'from here on everything is done from the receiver'.
RXV2-0.9.503-banner-wording: Calibrate-page banner reworded: from here on everything is done from your phone via the receiver.
RXV2-0.9.504-servo-power-warning: Wiring and Servos pages warn: do not power the servos until their frequency/pulse width and the BEC voltage are set - wrong settings can damage them.
RXV2-0.9.505-blades-on-step: New wizard step before Back up: blades back on, check main and tail pitch with a gauge, sweep full travel for mechanical issues.
RXV2-0.9.506-cyclic-balance: Travel extents: cyclic gain split into separate roll and pitch gains so the two axes can be balanced against the pitch gauge (8 vs 10 degrees is now fixable).
RXV2-0.9.507-banner-visible: Travel page's sticky status banner (SWASH HELD etc.) now sticks below the floating buttons instead of hiding behind them.
RXV2-0.9.508-gain-beside-hold: The Bench-measure card now carries the current axis's cyclic gain in a green box beside the Hold button (same value as Calibration, kept in step both ways) - measure and adjust on one screen.
RXV2-0.9.509-protocol-diet: Throttle/arming channels leave the Protocol page (the Transmitter-channels save now tells the receiver too); wave channels move to Receiver settings with their Test button.
RXV2-0.9.510-rescue-floating-save: Rescue page's Save button floats at the bottom of the screen (same bar as Travel extents) - no more scrolling to save.
RXV2-0.9.511-back-remembers: The floating back arrow now returns to the menu you actually came from (A la carte vs wizard) - it remembers the hub you navigated through.
RXV2-0.9.512-rf-button-name: Front-screen button renamed: Rotorflight setup and Wizard.
RXV2-0.9.513-help-bubbles: Press-and-hold help bubbles: touch any dotted-underlined label (governor, PIDs, rates, travel, servos - about 90 so far) and a plain-English explanation appears; lift your finger and it goes.
RXV2-0.9.514-bubble-polish: Help bubbles: no more iOS drag-ghost on finger movement, bubbles sit well clear of the finger, and ~20 more added (tail travel, battery divider, gear ratio, switch cards, every Transmitter-channels row).
RXV2-0.9.515-bubble-above: Help bubbles always appear ABOVE the finger (pinned to the top edge when the label is high on the screen) - never below.
RXV2-0.9.516-timeout-bubbles: Throttle-hold vs autorotation timeout bubbles now spell out the difference: ordinary throttle chop vs deliberate auto with bail-out.
RXV2-0.9.517-bailout-findable: Governor page now says plainly: bail-out is enabled by Auto throttle above 0 - there is no separate switch (note beside the autorotation timeout + a fuller bubble).
RXV2-0.9.518-bubble-hint: Wizard opens with a self-demonstrating note: underlined term? Put your finger on it for an explanation - and the note's own underline is a live example.
RXV2-0.9.519-clean-checklist: Wizard checklist decluttered: each step is just its underlined title - press and hold for a fuller explanation than the old subtext ever gave.
RXV2-0.9.520-hint-on-hub: The help-bubble explanation moves from the wizard to the Rotorflight front page - it applies to everything Rotorflight.
RXV2-0.9.521-tidy-rows: First-time basics, Rescue and Servos pages decluttered: every row is just its underlined title - press for a fuller explanation (43 rows converted).
RXV2-0.9.522-gear-dedup: Gear-ratio pages lose the paragraph that duplicated the label's help bubble.
RXV2-0.9.523-alacarte-alpha: A la carte menu sorted alphabetically - random-access choices are easiest to find in ABC order.
RXV2-0.9.524-alpha-subtitle: A la carte subtitle says 'In alphabetical order' (the old 'roughly in setup order' was no longer true).
RXV2-0.9.525-help-audit: Help screens audited against the current behaviour: wizard step numbers, alphabetical A la carte, selector bars with nothing to drag, divider-based Arm/Rescue, no x on Bank/Rates, Hello-wave in Receiver settings, selector cards on Switches.
RXV2-0.9.526-fourth-task: The computer session now lists FOUR tasks: firmware, serial port, select CRSF (new - without it there is no communication), Telemetry ON.
RXV2-0.9.527-unbrickable: Computer page gains the stuck-flash rescue card: BOOT button + USB = DFU, full chip erase, flash again - and the charge-only-cable trap explained.
RXV2-0.9.528-govmode-bubble: Governor-mode bubble corrected to RF 2.3's real modes (OFF/LIMIT/DIRECT/ELECTRIC/NITRO) - ELECTRIC is the right choice for electric helis; the old text used RF1 names.
RXV2-0.9.529-timings-in-seconds: Governor timings now displayed in SECONDS (converted to Rotorflight's tenths on the wire) - the tenths trap caused a 40-second spool-up on the Goblin's second flight.
RXV2-0.9.530-scorpion-readout: NEW (beta): ESC settings page reads a Scorpion Tribunus through the flight controller - every setting in plain English, no cables, no Windows. Read-only until hardware-verified; Release button reboots the ESC so telemetry returns.
RXV2-0.9.531-escprog-link: The wizard's ESC page now links straight to the Scorpion readout (beta) - it was only in A la carte.
RXV2-0.9.532-no-starve: FLIGHT-SAFETY: MSP waits (web/BLE config requests) now keep the radio and channel output running - an erroring request could starve the FC into rhythmic failsafe twitches (found live during the first Scorpion read attempt).
RXV2-0.9.533-esc-write: Scorpion ESC settings can now be CHANGED from the phone (beta): edit any field, Save writes only what changed and reads the ESC back to verify; Release reboots ESC + FC. Fixes: long MSP writes (84-byte ESC blob) were silently dropped (now chunked over CRSF); FC "MSP error" replies fail fast (502) instead of a 1.2 s timeout; battery-ritual guidance for the ESC listen window.
RXV2-0.9.534-escprog-route: Fix: the ESC settings page was never routed on the receiver itself (404 since 0.9.530 - only the phone apps served it). Ships the same Scorpion editor as 0.9.533.
RXV2-0.9.535-esc-wire-switches: First-time basics: new Two-way ESC talk (half-duplex) and ESC pin swap switches next to the ESC telemetry protocol - the Scorpion editor needs both on a Nexus X (its ESC pad is the UART RX pin). Verified-write like the rest of the page.
RXV2-0.9.551-throttle-parked: Governor pages now warn when the transmitter throttle sat below 100 % while armed (the head runs stable but slow and bank changes do nothing) - the receiver learns the throttle channel and governor mode from Rotorflight itself. New 'Governor controls the spool-up (PID spool-up)' switch in the governor profile. No more swash twitches: the event log is saved append-only and never while armed. Loop stalls now name the call that caused them.
RXV2-0.9.552-quiet-landing: Quieter event log: no false 'FC lost' after every flight (the FC probe pauses in the air; it now gets a fresh 10 s after landing) and one 'Swap unbilled' breadcrumb per 5 s instead of seven after every TX-off. Firmware only - pages unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.553-copy-bank: New 'Copy a bank' page (Rotorflight hub 4th door + A la carte): PIDs, PID+, rescue, rates and governor gains from one bank to another in ONE tap, saved, read back and verified byte for byte; each bank keeps its own head speed unless you tick 'Head speed too'; refused while armed; flight controller returned to the bank it was on. (Per-page 'Copy to Profile (Bank)' at the bottom of the PIDs / PID+ / Rates / Governor pages is unchanged.) Pages only - firmware behaviour unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.554-fs-wipe-on-fail: Safer updates: if the web-files (pages) download dies part-way (weak WiFi, power lost), the receiver now wipes the half-written pages instead of booting on them - a half-written page store hung the Goblin's receiver until a power cycle (2026-09-03). A wiped receiver still works fully from the app; run the update again to put its pages back. Backups and flights are carried across as before. Firmware only - pages unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.555-copybank-route: Fix: the Copy-a-bank page (Rotorflight > Copy a bank) opened fine in the app but gave 'not found' in a web browser on the receiver's own pages - the firmware was missing the link for it. Firmware only - pages unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.564-msp52-bug: Fix for the missing volts and RPM after a save: a Rotorflight 4.6 bug - its adjustments list (MSP 52) is too big for its receiver-link buffer and the overflow wipes its own telemetry setup. The receiver now never asks for that list, refuses it from any app or script, spots any oversize answer and puts the saved-good telemetry setup back before any save. Also refused: writes that arrive with no data, factory reset and motor test over the link.
RXV2-0.9.565-restore-counts: Backup & restore page: the finishing line now says what a restore actually did - 'Checked N settings - the model already had every one. Nothing was written' when nothing differed, or how many were written and verified (needs app 4.17 / Android 4.09 for the counts). The 'keep the transmitter OFF' warning disappears when the run is over.
RXV2-0.9.566-restore-names: Restore from phone now names what it wrote (up to four items, then a count) and the Back up / Restore result stays on screen until the next run instead of vanishing after a few seconds. Needs app 4.18 (iPhone) / 4.10 (Android) for the names.
RXV2-0.9.567-bank-putback: Banks go back to the transmitter's switch after a phone session. Rotorflight only re-applies a bank switch when the switch moves, so a tuning page that left the flight controller on another bank was flown on that bank until the switch moved. Now the receiver notes the switch's PID and rates banks before a page's first bank select, and 5 s after the phone goes quiet (transmitter off, disarmed) puts them back - and saves them as the boot banks if the session had saved on another bank. Never under a live transmitter (the switch owns the banks then; the event log says where the FC was left). Pages and apps see no difference: a request that arrives after a put-back gets its own bank re-selected first.
RXV2-0.9.568-bank-putback2: Bank put-back, bench-proven on the Goblin and polished: a put-back no longer forgets which bank the phone had chosen (so a read arriving after a put-back really does get the phone's bank re-selected first), a save marks the flight controller's bank as unknown until re-read (Rotorflight re-applies the switch by itself right after every save), and the event log now says 'Boot banks saved back for the switch' when only the boot bank needed fixing.
RXV2-0.9.569-card-wiggle: Two of Malcolm's suggestions. (1) The Rotorflight page's telemetry-speed card is now one quiet line - 'Telemetry: fast' - with the explanation under your finger (press and hold the underlined words), the Use standard / Use fast button as before. (2) The servo wiggle that announces 'the phone can connect' now also happens after a landing with the transmitter still on: as soon as the model is disarmed and the head speed reads zero, the chosen channel wiggles (a wiggle on a coasting rotor would yaw the model, so it waits for the stop - up to 90 s; without RPM telemetry, 30 s after disarming). Aborted wiggles now put the channel back exactly where it was.
RXV2-0.9.570-arm-fast: Auto fly mode now switches Bluetooth and WiFi off half a second after the arm switch goes on (it was 3 s, which looked as if the motor switch did it). Same half-second bounce filter as the disarm side.
RXV2-0.9.571-copy-hs: Copy a bank: new tick 'Adjust gains for the target bank's head speed'. Tune the middle bank, copy it outwards, and the copied P, I, D, feedforward and boost gains are scaled by the two banks' head speeds (control power grows with head speed squared): down fully for a faster bank, up more gently and never more than 25 % for a slower one. A note under the tick shows the change before you copy; the result names it afterwards. Malcolm's idea, 2026-09-05.
RXV2-0.9.572-arm-aux6: Arming channel learned from Rotorflight is now right: Rotorflight has five control channels, so its AUX1 is channel 6, not 5. Before this the receiver could pick the throttle channel as the arm switch, so 'armed' meant 'motor on' - radios went off with the motor and the landing wiggle came at motor-off while still armed. Check Receiver settings if you set the arming channel by hand.
RXV2-0.9.573-gov-noreload: Governor profile page: the 'Reload from flight controller' button is gone (it sat under the Spool-up card and got hit by mistake); switching banks re-reads the bank anyway.
RXV2-0.9.574-noreload: The PIDs, PID + and Rates pages lose their 'Reload from flight controller' button too (switching banks re-reads). The Governor (global) page keeps its one - it has no banks.
RXV2-0.9.575-start-slider: Governor page: a slider 'How hard should it start?' from very gentle to very fierce sets spool-up time, handover throttle and startup time together (gentle = full head speed in 40 s with handover 10 %, fierce = 10 s and 25 %), and saving can switch PID spool-up on in every bank so the torque is even all the way up. The numbers stay visible underneath. Malcolm's idea, 2026-09-06.
RXV2-0.9.576-feel-sliders: Two more plain-English controls, numbers still visible underneath. Rates page: 'How agile?' - a Docile-to-Acrobatic slider sets the top rotation speeds (roll and pitch 120 to 500 deg/s, yaw 150 to 600) and a Soft-centre-to-Direct slider sets the expo on all three axes (Rotorflight rates type). PIDs page: 'Feel' - Cyclic and Tail sliders from softer to sharper scale this bank's P, I, D and feedforward together by up to 30 %, relative to what was loaded; wobbles or shakes = softer, sluggish or mushy = sharper; after a save the sliders return to centre.
RXV2-0.9.577-easy-tuning: New in À la carte: 'Easy tuning' - every plain-English slider in one place (how hard it starts, how agile, softer/sharper feel), a link under each to the page with the numbers, one Save that writes only what changed and verifies it. And the sliders now work backwards on the Governor, Rates and PIDs pages: type a number by hand and the slider moves to match.
RXV2-0.9.578-slider-help: Press and hold a slider's heading (Easy tuning, Governor, Rates, PIDs pages) to see exactly which numbers it moves and by how much; the Easy tuning help page lists them too.
RXV2-0.9.579-back-trail: The back arrow now walks back through the last few pages you actually visited (up to six), instead of guessing the menu you came from. Going back pops the trail; a link that loops back to an earlier page shortens it.
RXV2-0.9.580-field-fixes: Two field fixes from the Goblin's first flight-test morning. (1) After a flight away from home WiFi, switching the transmitter off parked the flight-controller wire for the failsafe lamp while the phone was still connected over Bluetooth, so every Rotorflight read answered 'did not respond' until the receiver was rebooted. The wire now stays connected whenever Bluetooth config is up, and a phone request re-attaches it in any case. (2) The cell count read from Rotorflight was taken from the wrong byte (its battery STATE), which showed the 12S pack as '3S · 15 V/cell' on the Black box; the real count is read now. Also: the RealFlight controls page title no longer hides under the header buttons.
RXV2-0.9.581-whole-seconds: On the V1 transmitter the governor timings (spool-up, spool-down, speed-change/tracking, recovery, throttle-hold and autorotation timeouts) are now WHOLE SECONDS: 4 means four seconds. Rotorflight keeps them in tenths, and the transmitter's plain numbers made 4 mean 0.4 s. A half-second value saved from the transmitter rounds to the nearest second. The phone pages were already in seconds. Also corrects the governor-mode help text (DIRECT = throttle passed through with the ramps, for an ESC that governs by itself). Includes 0.9.580: the flight-controller wire stays connected after a field flight with the transmitter off, and the cell count is read from the right byte.
RXV2-0.9.582-backup-banks: Backup fix: 'the flight controller changed bank mid-backup' with the transmitter OFF. The receiver remembered the bank a phone last selected and quietly put the flight controller back on it before the next bank read, even when the phone had since asked the flight controller which bank it was on and started a fresh backup from there. The phone saw the move and gave up, leaving the flight controller on the wrong bank, so the next attempt failed the same way. Now a phone that reads the bank status is taken at its word. Includes 0.9.580 and 0.9.581.
RXV2-0.9.583-find-a-setting: NEW: Find a setting. Tap one and the page opens with that setting glowing for a few seconds. The index is built from the pages themselves, so it always matches this receiver. Includes 0.9.580-0.9.582.
RXV2-0.9.584-search-tidy: Find a setting: a stray '_head' entry (an include file, not a page) removed from the index. Otherwise as 0.9.583.
RXV2-0.9.585-search-everywhere: Find a setting is now a magnifier button beside the ? on every page, so a search is one tap away wherever you are; the menu buttons for it are gone. Page titles sit below the button row on every page.
RXV2-0.9.586-search-spacing: Find a setting: menu entries no longer run their title into their subtitle ("Backup & restorethe whole setup"). Otherwise as 0.9.585.
RXV2-0.9.589-slider-centres: Sliders that re-centre. Every plain-English slider (start hardness, agility, stick feel, cyclic and tail softer/sharper, on the Governor, Rates, PIDs and Easy tuning pages) now works relative to the numbers the model had at your last backup: the centre is 'what I have now', the ends are half and double (or 35 expo either way, or 30 % on the gains). RXV2-0.9.591-dongle-wire: Dongle mode: the receiver's status now counts the bytes, frames and CRC errors on the flight-controller wire, so a silent flight controller can be told from a wiring or port-setting mistake. Otherwise as 0.9.590.

RXV2-0.9.597-hsi-labels: PIDs page: the row that was called 'HSI off' is the O gain (how strongly the high-speed trim builds up) and is now labelled 'HSI gain (O)'; the PID+ page's 'high-speed trim cap (HSI offset limit)' is the ceiling in degrees. RXV2-0.9.610-keep-close: Backup page: 'Keep the phone close to the model until the backup is complete' is the first line while a backup runs, and a struggling link shows live ('weak link, move closer' once three reads have needed a second try; apps 4.52/4.44 report it). RXV2-0.9.619-usb-jumbo: Dongle over USB: big replies (255 bytes and more, e.g. the adjustments list) are now parsed in Rotorflight's real jumbo-frame order - size, command, then the 16-bit length. Includes 0.9.618.

RXV2-0.9.625-knob-switch: In-flight adjustments: the choice reads just Knob or Switch and the page loses its introduction - what they mean is in the help (Malcolm 2026-09-11: 'keep this page as simple as possible'). Includes 0.9.624.

RXV2-0.9.631-bank-list: In-flight adjustments: the 'What it changes' list itself now offers every setting per bank - 'Yaw P gain in bank 1', 'in bank 2' ... and 'in the bank in use' - grouped by bank; no separate bank choice. Garbled labels fixed (collective, cutoff, altitude). Includes 0.9.630.

RXV2-0.9.634-rate-units: In-flight adjustments: the Rate entries now show and save the same numbers as the Rates page (Rotorflight stores Rate/5 for its own rates type, Rate/10 for the older types; the page reads the rates type from the flight controller and converts both ways). RXV2-0.9.638-usb-wording: Help on In-flight adjustments and Command line: the USB cable runs from the dongle to the flight controller, not to a laptop (Malcolm: some might assume it needs the laptop). Includes 0.9.637.
RXV2-0.9.639-usb-on-receiver: A RECEIVER now hosts the flight controller on its USB socket exactly as the dongle does (Malcolm 2026-09-11: 'Yes let's do it'): a USB-C cable from the receiver to the flight controller gives the app every Rotorflight setting (the full adjustments read, In-flight adjustments, the Command line), while the CRSF line keeps carrying channels and telemetry. RXV2-0.9.645-cable-wording: The USB-only pages now say 'connect a USB cable between the flight controller's USB socket and the receiver's USB socket' (Malcolm, after the successful Goblin test with the transmitter on). Includes 0.9.644.
RXV2-0.9.646-remove-saves: In-flight adjustments: Remove asks 'Remove ... from the flight controller?' and saves straight away (Malcolm 2026-09-11: did not realise Save was still needed); any other edit turns the Save button orange with 'unsaved changes' until saved. Includes 0.9.645.
RXV2-0.9.647-ports: New Ports page (Rotorflight's Ports tab): each flight-controller UART gets one plain choice - nothing, receiver (CRSF, SBUS or IBUS), dongle on a wire (MSP 115200), ESC telemetry, S.Port telemetry, GPS or blackbox; other setups are kept as they are; one receiver port only; Save writes the ports and the receiver protocol, saves, restarts the flight controller and waits for it. With this, a new receiver never needs the configurator: the port is set from the phone over USB. Includes 0.9.646.
RXV2-0.9.648-nexus-labels: Ports page: on a RadioMaster Nexus or Nexus-X (the board name the flight controller reports) the ports carry the socket names printed on the board - Port A (UART 4), Port B (UART 6), Port C (UART 3), TELEM (UART 2) and S.BUS (UART 1) on the Nexus-X; DSM/S.BUS on the original. Other boards keep UART numbers. Help explains the letters. Includes 0.9.647.
RXV2-0.9.649-alacarte-order: A la carte: In-flight adjustments sits in its alphabetical place (after Governor). Includes 0.9.648.
RXV2-0.9.650-back-scroll: Back returns to where you were: a long list (A la carte, Find a setting, any page) remembers its scroll position when you leave it and puts it back when you come back by the back arrow or a back gesture. A fresh visit still starts at the top. Includes 0.9.649.
RXV2-0.9.651-adj-offline-copy: In-flight adjustments: without the USB cable the page shows the set it last read over USB (kept per model on the phone), greyed and not changeable, with the time it was read; the live switch marker still moves over the radio link. Includes 0.9.650.
RXV2-0.9.652-greyed-darker: Greyed (read-only) controls on In-flight adjustments and the Command line stay readable: dark text at 80 percent instead of 45. Includes 0.9.651.
RXV2-0.9.653-recording-banner: A replayed recording (Review: <model> in the app's list) now says so at the top of every page: 'Recording of <model> - nothing here is live. To connect, use Load another model on the front page.' Includes 0.9.652.
RXV2-0.9.654-review-fixes: From a critical pass over the day's work: In-flight adjustments never switches flight-controller banks while the transmitter is on (the boxes fill only for the bank in use; flip the switch for another); a Remove whose save fails reloads the page from the flight controller and says 'Not removed'; Save shows 'Writing line N of 43'; a receiver whose line to the flight controller carries no MSP (SBUS, IBUS, PPM, or FC telemetry off) answers 'needs the USB cable' instead of a timeout; the Ports warning covers the dongle's own port. Includes 0.9.653.
RXV2-0.9.655-filters: New Filters page (Rotorflight's Filters tab): gyro lowpass 1 and 2 (type and cutoff), rotor-speed (RPM) notch preset and lowest frequency, dynamic notches (count, width, range) and the two fixed notches; read-modify-write of MSP 92/93, takes effect at once. The help explains what each filter does and how to read the Blackbox Explorer's frequency view to see which filter is needed. Includes 0.9.654.
RXV2-0.9.656-two-wires: Help: 'Two wires, everything' - the receiver lead carries flying and the everyday pages; the USB-C cable adds the configurator's own channel (every setting, any size, command line, ports, factory reset, black box); a transmitter's Lua scripts have only the slow 320-byte CRSF tunnel. Said on the Rotorflight menu help and in every help screen's Ways to connect, which no longer calls the app Apple-only. Includes 0.9.655.
RXV2-0.9.657-cable: Help (Rotorflight menu, Setup's USB socket, every Ways-to-connect footer): buy a SHORT USB-C cable, about 12 cm, right-angled at the flight controller if you can, and make sure it is a data cable - many short leads only charge. Includes 0.9.656.
RXV2-0.9.658-help-corner: The ? and search circles sit 2.6em further in from the top-right corner, clear of the app's small X on the demo and review screens (iPad mis-taps). Includes 0.9.657.
RXV2-0.9.659-usb-first-time: Before you start: a computer only to flash the firmware; with the USB cable the Ports page does the rest - choosing 'receiver' for a port now also switches on serial receiver mode and telemetry (features 3 + 10, read-modify-write) in the same Save, so a brand-new flight controller never needs the configurator's Receiver tab. Configurator steps kept as the no-cable alternative. New-heli wizard step reworded. Includes 0.9.658.
RXV2-0.9.660-two-wires-card: Before you start opens with 'First, get a short USB-C data cable': connect both wires - the lead flies and carries the everyday pages, the USB cable is the configurator's own channel (every setting, Ports, In-flight adjustments, command line, factory reset, black box); about 12 cm, right-angled if possible, must carry data. Without it the computer does the port/CRSF/telemetry and the USB-only pages stay out of reach. Includes 0.9.659.
RXV2-0.9.661-vibration-check: VIBRATION CHECK: the receiver (or dongle) reads the flight controller's black box over the USB cable (MSP 70/71, 512-byte chunks, one per loop pass), decodes Rotorflight 4.6's log format on the fly (src/BlackboxDecode.h, spec in BLACKBOX-FORMAT.md), accumulates Welch spectra of the gyro before and after the filters plus a head-speed-locked order spectrum, and the new page (Flight recorder → Vibration check, or the full list) names the lines (rotor, blades, motor, tail, or something loose), says in one line which filter to change and applies it (rotor-speed notch preset, lowest rotor frequency, fixed notch 1/2, dynamic notches, Lowpass 1). USB only, transmitter off, disarmed; /api/msp answers 503 while it runs; the heartbeat and TX-param machine stand down. Host-tested on synthetic logs (dev/bbcheck_test.sh). Includes 0.9.660.
RXV2-0.9.662-vibration-check-safe: Vibration check made safe before real flying (review + Malcolm's rules): the check owns the MSP link - every other sender stands down and /api/msp answers 503; arming is re-asked every second over USB; MSP 70 flag bits corrected (READY=1, SUPPORTED=2 - the recorder page had them the other way round too); a late reply re-arms instead of re-sending; PSRAM only; float maths. Decoder: the two TAG8_8SVB groups (sensors / temperatures) never merge, a header straight after a truncated log is recognised, time predictors in wrapping arithmetic, no 4.8 kB stack temporary. Analyser keeps the newest log that FLEW (a bench arm after landing no longer replaces the flight). Page: Apply is bounded (Lowpass 1 never below 60 and never raised, fixed notches 80-1000 Hz, dynamic notches 0-8), refused while armed or the rotor turns or on an unverified Rotorflight, read back and compared, Undo, ONE change per flight; filter advice only when the log has Gyro raw + Gyro + Head speed. Includes 0.9.661.
RXV2-0.9.663-check-fast: Vibration check: the armed gate no longer aborts the check before the flight controller has answered (and never forces the shared armed flag every page reads); reads 4096-byte chunks where the FC allows, through the check's own PSRAM buffer.
RXV2-0.9.665-check-goblin: Vibration check, corrected by the Goblin's own flight: it advised 'set the rotor-speed notches to high' for a once-per-rev that Rotorflight's NORMAL preset already notches - the change would have done nothing. The check now knows what each preset really notches (rpmFilterPreset[] in rpm_filter.c: main harmonics 1-2-4 low, 1-4 normal, 1-6 high, tail 1 / 1-2 / 1-2, plus the main motor) and only advises a preset that genuinely adds the harmonic; a strong once-per-rev is reported as blade tracking and balance, with no filter button. Attenuation is measured over a wider window so a narrow rotor notch is not mistaken for a useless one. The 90-second Goblin flight is now a regression fixture (dev/goblin_flight_*.json). Includes 0.9.664.
RXV2-0.9.664-check-window: Vibration check reads the last 12 MB of the black box (the newest flight or two) instead of the whole memory, widening itself if that holds no log, and shows a time remaining; the page says so and offers Erase. Measured throughput 62-66 kB/s.
RXV2-0.9.666-check-watchdog: Two safety nets before the Goblin flies: bbCheckActive (which stands every other MSP sender down) can never outlive the check that set it - the idle tick clears it and says so in the log; and a check that somehow ran past 20 minutes hands the flight controller back. Nothing in the flight path changed: Radio.h, Channels.h, Output.h, Telemetry.h and FlightLog.h are untouched since before the vibration check existed. Includes 0.9.665.
RXV2-0.9.667-banks-first: FLIGHT SAFETY, found by the pre-flight review: a vibration check stands the bank put-back down for its whole run, so if a phone session had left the flight controller on a different PID bank and the transmitter came on during the check, the put-back was abandoned and the model would have flown on the phone's bank. A check now refuses to start while the banks are still held, and while any page has talked to the flight controller in the last 5 seconds (a restore is many requests with gaps); the page waits and retries by itself, so it is invisible. Also: the 20-minute cap now bounds the whole run, not each widened pass. Includes 0.9.666.
RXV2-0.9.668-armed-recheck: FLIGHT SAFETY: the vibration check's once-a-second 'is it armed?' re-check never actually ran while the black box was streaming - it lived only on the idle path, and a healthy stream re-arms the next read immediately, so the flight controller's armed word was read once at the start and then frozen. On a receiver the transmitter test still covered it; on a DONGLE nothing did. All 'what next?' decisions now go through one place that gives the armed re-check its turn. Also: the idle watchdog now leaves exactly the state stopLink() leaves (a latched mspAsyncFunc would have confused the transmitter-parameter machine), and the serial MSP parser is reset when a read times out and whenever the USB device comes or goes, so one dropped byte cannot hold it open for a whole 4 kB reply. Includes 0.9.667.
RXV2-0.9.669-bank-handover: Defence in depth on the bank hazard: a check already cannot start while the flight controller's banks are still held (0.9.667), but the vibration check's stand-down in bankPutBackTick now sits BELOW the transmitter hand-over instead of above it, so a transmitter switched on during a check still reaches the branch that releases the hold and records where the flight controller was left. Only the MSP work waits. And when the link is handed back, an owed put-back is attempted at once instead of after the two-second back-off. Includes 0.9.668.
RXV2-0.9.670-memory-card: Vibration check page: a Black box memory card of its own - a bar and a plain 'X of Y used (Z%)' line, and an 'Erase all flight logs' button right there, refused while armed or with the rotor turning and confirmed first. When the memory is over half full it says how much time erasing would save, because that is where you notice it. The Flight recorder page keeps its own copy of both. Includes 0.9.669.
RXV2-0.9.671-flight-review: See the flight, not just its vibration. The check now decodes head speed, the governor's wanted speed, throttle, battery volts and current, roll and pitch, ESC temperature and motor RPM as it reads, and the page shows them as a stack of traces sharing one time axis, with arming, governor changes and rescue marked - plus a plain-English summary ('Head speed averaged 1325 rpm, dipping to 1270. The governor asked for 1300, so it held to within 25 rpm. Battery 25.0 V down to 23.4 V, sagging to 22.8 V under load.'). A link to What to record on the Flight recorder page sits on the check page, since that is where you notice a field is missing. Includes 0.9.670.
RXV2-0.9.672-keep-checks: Every finished check is now kept on the phone - the last six per model, about 30 kB each - and any of them can be opened again with no cable and no helicopter. So erasing the black box costs nothing, and a flight can be looked at again after a filter change. A kept check is clearly marked and can change nothing; run a new one for that. Page only, no firmware behaviour changed. Includes 0.9.671.
RXV2-0.9.673-help-back: Every help screen now has a Back button at the TOP that stays there while you scroll, so opening one by mistake no longer means scrolling to the bottom to get out (Malcolm asked). Got it stays at the bottom for anyone who reads to the end, tapping outside still closes, and Escape now does too. The help panel is a solid colour, as everything else on these pages is. Includes 0.9.672.
RXV2-0.9.674-help-arrow: The help screen's way out is now the SAME round back arrow as every page, in the same top-left corner, instead of the wide bar 0.9.673 used. It floats above the overlay so it is there however far the help is scrolled. Got it stays at the bottom, tapping outside and Escape still work. The test compares its size, shape, colour and arrow against the page back button rule by rule. Includes 0.9.673.
RXV2-0.9.675-help-round: The help back button really is the round arrow now. 0.9.674 gave it the class the wide green Got-it button uses, and since that rule comes later in the stylesheet it won on every shared property - so it rendered as a full-width teal bar. It now has its own class, declared after, and the panel starts below it exactly as a page's content starts below its floating buttons (the button is 3em of its own 1.55em font, so 4.65em tall, not 3em). Verified by screenshot in a headless browser, not by reading the CSS. Includes 0.9.674.
RXV2-0.9.676-cable-advice: Cable advice matches what actually works on the model: the shortest cable you can get, right-angled at BOTH ends if possible, tied down and left in - it costs nothing in the air because the receiver stops talking over USB the moment the radio link is live. Said in the Ways-to-connect footer, the Rotorflight menu help and Setup's USB socket bullet; the website carries the fitted photo. Includes 0.9.675.
RXV2-0.9.677-cable-part: The help now names the exact cable: a Chenyang CY-UC-088-0.07M, 70 mm, flat, USB-C at both ends with both plugs right-angled, USB 2.0 data, 65 W, on Amazon. Any short one will do so long as it carries data. The website says the same and carries the photo of it fitted. Includes 0.9.676.
RXV2-0.9.678-ports-link: Before you start, step 2 now has an Open Ports button, so the one page it tells you to use is one tap away instead of something to go and find. Includes 0.9.677.
RXV2-0.9.679-help-links: Where a help screen tells you to use another page, it now offers it: the Filters help has Vibration check and Flight recorder buttons, and In-flight adjustments links the Switches page where the bank switch is set. Includes 0.9.678.
RXV2-0.9.680-cli-leave: Command line: Leave without saving now leaves - it closes the session and then goes where the back arrow goes, instead of leaving you on a dead page to press Back yourself. Both buttons are disabled once the session is closed, which is what printed 'the command line was not open' when they were pressed again. Save and restart deliberately stays, because the flight controller is restarting and the message says so. Includes 0.9.679.
RXV2-0.9.681-black-box: Rotorflight's Flight recorder is now called Black box (Flight recorder), and sits under B in the a-la-carte list where you look for it. The page, its help and everything that points at it say Black box; the search index keeps both meanings apart, since the receiver has a Black box page of its own. Includes 0.9.680.
RXV2-0.9.682-receiver-log: Two things were both called the black box. The receiver's own is now the RECEIVER LOG - what this receiver saw: live status, the radio link, past flights and events - on the front page, in its title and help, and in search. Black box (Flight recorder) keeps that name for the flight controller's recording, and now carries a 'Not this one?' card pointing across to the Receiver log; the Receiver log points back. Includes 0.9.681.
RXV2-0.9.683-log-under-blackbox: The Receiver log is offered plainly at the foot of Black box (Flight recorder) - no heading, no explaining - and is off the front page. It reappears on the front page only for a receiver with no Rotorflight, which would otherwise have no Black box page to reach it through. Includes 0.9.682.
RXV2-0.9.684-read-black-box: The Vibration check is now called READ BLACK BOX, because that is what it does - it grew from filter advice into the whole flight - and it lives inside the black box area instead of as a separate entry in the list. Black box (Flight recorder) leads with it, and the Receiver log sits at the foot of the same page, so everything about recordings is in one place. Includes 0.9.683.
RXV2-0.9.685-button-gap: Read black box: the two buttons touched - the link above had no bottom margin and the button below had none at all. Checked by screenshot this time, not by reading the CSS. Includes 0.9.684.
RXV2-0.9.686-log-colour: The Receiver log button at the foot of Black box was grey, which reads as disabled. It is now the Receiver log's own blue - bright, and clear of the green above it. Includes 0.9.685.
RXV2-0.9.687-fewer-settings: Two settings left the Setup menu, because the receiver already knows the answers. It works out for itself whether it is a dongle or a receiver, and a flight controller plugged into its USB socket is adopted with no setting to turn on. A board that IS a dongle still shows its own button for the name and serial speed, and that is also where a receiver whose radios failed to start can force itself back to being a receiver. Also: in the new-helicopter wizard, the Back up step opened the Setup page instead of Backup & restore. Includes 0.9.686.
RXV2-0.9.688-usb-advice: Three pages still told you to turn the USB socket on in Setup - a button that 0.9.687 removed, because the receiver now works the socket out for itself. They now say to restart the receiver, which is the only thing that can actually be wrong. Found in an App Store screenshot. Includes 0.9.687.
RXV2-0.9.689-dev-host: The built-in address for a local firmware server was the developer's own Mac name. Two reasons to change it: it published a private machine name in every release, and any computer on your network answering to that name could have offered your receiver firmware. It is now a neutral name that nothing answers to by default, so updates come from messiter.com unless you set your own. Includes 0.9.688.
RXV2-0.9.690-heli-3d: The rotating helicopter on the View channels page is much better looking. It now sits on a real shadow, the bodywork is glossy and catches the light, the metal parts look like metal, and you can see through the spinning rotor instead of it being a grey plate. Same model, properly lit. Includes 0.9.689.
RXV2-0.9.691-goblin-livery: The 3D helicopter now looks like a real model helicopter: orange shell with the white and black graphics, white boom and skids, orange tail fin, and a blunt rounded nose instead of the sharp cone. It also has two blades, as a Goblin does, rather than four. Includes 0.9.690.
RXV2-0.9.692-goblin-detail: The 3D helicopter is a proper model now. The nose bulge is gone - the whole shell is one smooth surface instead of spheres stuck together - and the front is shorter. The canopy stops behind the cabin, so you can see the black carbon frame, the motor, the servos and the battery, just as you can on the real thing. The boom carries GOBLIN lettering and a tail stabiliser, and the tail fin is swept rather than a square slab. Includes 0.9.691.
RXV2-0.9.693-goblin-match: The 3D helicopter now matches the real Goblin in the details that show: wide flat black landing-gear plates instead of wire legs, the big dark cut-out low in the canopy side with its white surround, GOBLIN 770 and SAB HELI DIVISION lettering along the shell, pale flashes and orange chevrons near the blade tips, and pitch links on the rotor head. Includes 0.9.692.
RXV2-0.9.694-tail-skid: The 3D helicopter's tail skid now rakes down and backwards with a black foot on the end, the way the real one does, so a tail-low landing would put the skid down rather than the tail blades. The landing skids have their black end caps, the tail rotor has two blades and its orange pitch bracket, and the tail stabiliser sits further aft. Includes 0.9.693.
RXV2-0.9.695-ldrc-livery: The 3D helicopter now carries our own name. The shell reads LDRC over LOCKDOWN RADIO CONTROL and the tail boom reads LDRC, in place of the manufacturer's name, which belongs to them. The shape is still modelled on a real machine; only the lettering has changed. Includes 0.9.694.
RXV2-0.9.696-tail-line: The 3D helicopter has lost the orange fin that stuck up from its tail, and the tail rotor now turns on the tail boom's own centreline instead of floating above it. The gearbox and tail skid moved down to match. Includes 0.9.695.
RXV2-0.9.697-tail-tidy: Three tidies to the 3D helicopter: the horizontal stabiliser at the back has gone, the tail rotor is a bit bigger, and two black posts that had been poking out of the belly have gone. Those posts were a mistake - a cross-tube that was never turned on its side, so it stood on its end. Includes 0.9.696.
RXV2-0.9.698-tail-clearance: On the 3D helicopter the tail skid now reaches further down, and the tail rotor is larger - its lowest point comes to just above the bottom of the skid, so the skid would touch first. Includes 0.9.697.
RXV2-0.9.699-stray-wires: A few stray wires now peek out of the back of the 3D helicopter's frame, the way nobody's loom is ever quite tucked in. Three leads, each with its own droop and deliberately not matching. Includes 0.9.698.
RXV2-0.9.700-wire-loops: The stray wires on the 3D helicopter are loops now: they come out of the frame a little way and go back in, instead of stopping in mid-air with a cut end. Includes 0.9.699.
RXV2-0.9.701-gear-joined: On the 3D helicopter the landing-gear supports now actually join up: they reach the skids below and go up into the frame above, instead of stopping just short of both. Includes 0.9.700.
RXV2-0.9.702-dongle-channels: View channels now works on a dongle. A dongle has no radio of its own, so it asks the flight controller what its receiver is giving it and shows those - the bars and the little helicopter prove the whole chain, from your transmitter through its receiver to the flight controller. It pauses while the model is armed. Includes 0.9.701.
RXV2-0.9.703-dongle-channels-fix: View channels really does work on a dongle now. 0.9.702 taught the dongle to read the channels and put the button back on the Setup menu, but the page itself still turned you away with 'Not on a dongle'. Includes 0.9.702.
RXV2-0.9.704-dongle-rxlog: On a dongle the Black box page no longer offers the Receiver log button. A dongle has no radio link, no battery sense and no flights of its own, so there was nothing behind it - and tapping it walked you into 'Not on a dongle'. Includes 0.9.703.
RXV2-0.9.705-cli-autoexit: Forgetting to leave the command line no longer breaks everything else. Leaving that page by any route - back, the front screen, or closing the app - now does what Leave without saving does. And if a command line is left open and untouched for a minute and a half, the receiver closes it for you. It never does that while the transmitter is on or the model is armed, because leaving restarts the flight controller. Includes 0.9.704.
RXV2-0.9.706-usb-after-update: The USB socket should now work straight after an update, without needing a second reboot. The restart was leaving the flight controller still thinking its USB port was open, so the receiver came back to a device that would not answer; it is now given a proper disconnect first. Each boot also records which version is running and from which half of the memory, on the Receiver log, so a firmware update that did not stick can be spotted. Includes 0.9.705.
RXV2-0.9.707-honest-errors: When something goes wrong applying telemetry settings you now get a reason instead of a browser message. 'The string did not match the expected pattern' was the phone's own wording for a reply it could not read; it now says what the receiver actually answered, or that it answered nothing. Includes 0.9.706.
RXV2-0.9.708-please-wait: The command line now shows a Please wait strip with a moving bar and the seconds counting up, so a slow command no longer looks like a frozen screen. After four seconds it adds that dump and diff are the slow ones. The telemetry buttons count the seconds too. Includes 0.9.707.
RXV2-0.9.710-reading-indicator: Every page that reads from the flight controller - PIDs, governor, rates, servos and the rest - now shows 'Reading from the flight controller' along the bottom with the seconds counting up, if it takes more than a moment. Quick reads show nothing, so it only appears when you would otherwise wonder. Includes 0.9.708.
RXV2-0.9.711-channels-stream: View channels should keep up with your sticks over Bluetooth again. The receiver only sends a channel update when nothing else is being asked of it, but the page had been asking constantly - so the fast updates never got a chance to start and the bars crawled. The page now leaves room. Includes 0.9.710.
RXV2-0.9.712-ble-loop: An important one. Serving a page over Bluetooth used to hold the receiver's main loop for about a fifth of a second at a time - long enough to miss around 47 control frames to the flight controller, on the bench with the transmitter on. It now hands out its Bluetooth work in 3 millisecond slices (1.2 while a transmitter is linked) and always returns to flying the model. Also: the Reading from the flight controller strip no longer sits on top of the Save and Back buttons. Includes 0.9.711.
RXV2-0.9.713-less-chatter: The app now asks the receiver far less often over Bluetooth. The status document it fetches is 4.4 kB, Bluetooth carries about 24 kB a second, and several parts of the app were each asking for it two or three times a second - so most of the link was spent on it and everything else queued behind. Those requests now share one answer, and pages poll every 1.5 seconds instead of twice a second. WiFi is unchanged. Includes 0.9.712.
RXV2-0.9.714-adaptive-poll: View channels now adapts. It asks briskly until the receiver's fast push actually starts working, and only then stands back to let the push do the work. Before, it always stood back - which was slower than it used to be whenever the push did not start. It can no longer be slower than it was. Includes 0.9.713.
RXV2-0.9.715-safety-gates: Safety review fixes. Capturing or clearing the failsafe positions is now refused while the model is armed - capturing on an armed model would have stored the arming switch ON as the failsafe position. Installing firmware is refused while the transmitter is on, because the receiver stops sending control frames for the whole download. Bringing the radios back after a flight now parks the output safely instead of restarting bare. And a dongle no longer writes control frames into the flight controller's settings port while waiting for a reply. Includes 0.9.714.
RXV2-0.9.716-dongle-power: The dongle's Wiring section now warns that if you also run a USB cable to the flight controller, the dongle's 5 V must come from the flight controller itself and not from a separate supply - the dongle puts 5 V down that cable, so a second supply would meet the flight controller's own 5 V through it. It also explains that D5 and D6 become a fallback once USB is in use. Includes 0.9.715.
RXV2-0.9.717-rf-update-hint: The Rotorflight page can now tell you when a newer Rotorflight has come out - the one job these pages cannot do for you. It says nothing at all unless there is something worth acting on, it tells you to back up first because flashing erases everything, and if the new release is one these pages have not been checked against yet it says the opposite: stay where you are, there is no hurry. Includes 0.9.716.
RXV2-0.9.718-rf-check-daily: The Rotorflight update check now happens once a day, on the first time you open the app that day, and never makes you wait for it - anything it already knows is shown at once and the check happens quietly behind. If it cannot reach the internet it tries again in an hour rather than giving up for the day. Includes 0.9.717.
RXV2-0.9.719-weak-wifi-choice: When the receiver's WiFi is weak, the Firmware page now says so before you start and offers Bluetooth instead - slower, but it does not depend on the weak signal. And if a WiFi install does crawl and fail, there is now a button to try again over Bluetooth rather than leaving you to work it out. The old firmware is untouched either way. Includes 0.9.718.
RXV2-0.9.720-patient-install: An install that was simply taking a long time was being reported as a failure. The page gave it two and a half minutes, which is plenty on a good signal and not nearly enough on a weak one. It now says 'still going' and keeps watching for another three minutes before it says anything went wrong - and if it cannot actually see the new version with its own eyes, it says so rather than claiming success. Includes 0.9.719.
